articles.title: Britain and the Pentagon told people to get ready in October. Now Costco is selling out of generators, and billionaires have ‘apocalypse insurance’
articles.summary: A string of tech outages has Costco members stocking up on rice, water, and generators. The buying started weeks before the outages did.
articles.body:
Costco shoppers are "pantry-loading" again. As of Sunday night, 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators on Costco's website were sold out, according to Mizuho Securities analyst David Bellinger. One of the sold-out models, a Kohler, runs about $7,000.

The last time Costco members bought like this was March 2020, when then-CFO Richard Galanti told investors the buying was "off the charts" across the U.S. On March 12 of that year, U.S. toilet paper sales were up 734% from the same day a year earlier.

This time the buying picked up after a run of tech failures that has kept people out of their email, grounded flights, and left bank customers unable to move money, and households are now spending to get ready for the next one. Bellinger told clients that consumer anxiety after the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stop for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up on social media is behind the buying. He raised his Costco price target to $1,150 from $1,100 and said Walmart and Sam's Club could see similar "pantry-loading lifts."

Costco CFO Gary Millerchip told Bloomberg that stronger sales of rice, canned goods, water, paper products, generators, and batteries came toward the end of October. Mizuho says Home Depot and Lowe's could sell more generators, too.

Smaller sellers are seeing the same thing. Survival Frog, which sells emergency food, radios, and other survival gear, saw sales jump 450% between Oct. 27 and Nov. 16 compared with prior weeks, founder and CEO Byron Walker told Axios . Most of the recent buyers were new customers, and food, led by canned meats, is the top seller, followed by radios, solar generators, battery packs, and water filters. Competitors saw similar trends, Walker said.

"You can't turn on the news without hearing about a new cyberattack or a tech meltdown," he said.

Costco's reported sales don't show the spike yet. U.S. comparable sales excluding gas rose 8.1% in the four weeks ended Nov. 1, according to Costco , the same pace as the first nine weeks of its fiscal year. Mizuho estimates U.S. growth sped up to 11% to 12% in the last week of October and into early November, and holiday shopping may be part of that.

The Federal Reserve's cash data covers only the week before the bank outages. Currency in circulation averaged about $2.5 trillion in the week ended Nov. 11, roughly 3% more than a year earlier, according to the Fed's weekly H.4.1 release . The next reading, covering the week of the Chase outage, comes out Thursday afternoon.

articles.title: Ações da Anthropic caem 8,5% um dia após estreia histórica na bolsa | G1
articles.standfirst: Queda ocorre em meio ao pessimismo dos investidores com o setor de inteligência artificial e às dúvidas sobre o retorno dos bilhões investidos na tecnologia.
articles.summary: Queda ocorre em meio ao pessimismo dos investidores com o setor de inteligência artificial e às dúvidas sobre o retorno dos bilhões investidos na tecnologia.
articles.body:
Placa da Anthropic , PBC (ANT) no One Times Square no dia em que a Anthropic realiza sua oferta pública inicial (IPO) na NASDAQ Market, em Nova York, EUA, em 19 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton

As ações da Anthropic, criadora do chatbot de inteligência artificial (IA) Claude, fecharam em queda de 8,5% nesta sexta-feira (20), a US$ 88,91 , um dia após a estreia histórica da empresa na bolsa de valores dos Estados Unidos.

O resultado aproximou os papéis dos US$ 83 fixados na oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês), em meio ao crescente pessimismo dos investidores em relação ao setor de IA.

Na quinta-feira (19), primeiro dia de negociação, as ações da empresa encerraram o pregão a US$ 97,17 . A abertura de capital movimentou US$ 93,5 bilhões, superando o recorde anterior de US$ 85,7 bilhões da SpaceX, de Elon Musk.

A estreia da Anthropic era vista como uma oportunidade de recuperar o entusiasmo dos investidores com as empresas de inteligência artificial. A queda das ações, porém, mostrou que nem mesmo o maior IPO da história foi suficiente para reverter a cautela que domina o setor.

O setor de IA tem enfrentado pressão no último mês, diante das crescentes preocupações de que os investimentos na tecnologia, que podem ultrapassar US$ 1 trilhão neste ano , segundo algumas estimativas, não estejam gerando retornos com rapidez suficiente.

O receio de obstáculos políticos à construção de centros de dados e a turbulência na liderança da fabricante de chips Nvidia também contribuíram para essas preocupações.

"A Anthropic perdeu força relativamente rápido. Não acho que os investidores acreditem que exista algo fundamentalmente errado com a empresa, sua administração ou seus negócios. Acho que eles estão apenas céticos em relação a esse mercado", afirmou Robert Pavlik, gestor sênior de portfólio da Dakota Wealth, à Reuters.

David Miller, diretor de investimentos da Catalyst Funds, disse à agência que os investidores "ainda acreditam na inteligência artificial, mas estão se tornando mais seletivos em relação ao preço que estão dispostos a pagar por esse crescimento".

O movimento também atingiu outras gigantes de tecnologia. Entre as chamadas Sete Magníficas, a Nvidia caiu cerca de 14% , enquanto a Meta recuou quase 6% , a Amazon perdeu aproximadamente 4% e a Microsoft encerrou o pregão em queda de 3%.

As fabricantes de semicondutores também registraram perdas. As ações da AMD e da Marvell Technology caíram cerca de 13% e 12%, respectivamente, enquanto a Intel recuou aproximadamente 8%.

Considerando o preço mais recente das ações, a Anthropic tinha um valor de mercado de US$ 1,2 trilhão nesta sexta-feira, calculado com base nos papéis atualmente em circulação.

Já a avaliação totalmente diluída, que considera também ações que poderão ser emitidas no futuro, como as vinculadas a opções e outros direitos, chegava a aproximadamente US$ 1,6 trilhão.

Na véspera, essa avaliação chegou a superar momentaneamente os US$ 2 trilhões , durante a estreia da companhia na bolsa.

"Defendemos a paciência em relação à Anthropic e recomendamos avaliar a empresa à medida que ela divulgar seus resultados como companhia aberta", afirmou à Reuters Kaush Amin, chefe de investimentos em mercados privados da US Bank Asset Management.

Ele acrescentou à agência que a avaliação atual da companhia "pressupõe anos de crescimento acelerado".

Em meio às dúvidas sobre as perspectivas do setor, as atenções agora se voltam para uma possível abertura de capital da OpenAI , outra líder em inteligência artificial. A operação poderá representar um novo teste para o interesse dos investidores.

Apesar da perspectiva de uma série de IPOs de grandes empresas de inteligência artificial e infraestrutura, muitas adiaram seus planos para 2027.

O IPO da Anthropic tem provocado comparações com o da SpaceX, de Elon Musk, cuja abertura de capital, realizada em junho, foi a segunda maior da história.

Embora as empresas tenham modelos de negócios diferentes, alguns investidores apontaram as fortes oscilações das ações da SpaceX nas semanas seguintes à sua estreia como motivo para ter cautela antes de comprar papéis da Anthropic imediatamente após sua abertura de capital.

"Haverá alguma volatilidade, assim como aconteceu com a SpaceX. Muita gente vai sentir medo de ficar de fora. Não acho que exista necessidade de entrar logo na primeira negociação", afirmou Rob Hackel, presidente-executivo da consultoria financeira e corretora RF Lafferty & Co.

As ações da SpaceX caíram quase 8% nesta sexta-feira.

Investidores individuais negociaram aproximadamente US$ 772 milhões em ações da Anthropic na quinta-feira, o maior volume registrado na estreia de um IPO desde que a Vanda Research começou a acompanhar esses dados, em 2012.

As fortes oscilações dos papéis deixaram os investidores divididos entre a possibilidade de recuperação e o risco de novas perdas. O início das negociações de opções sobre as ações, previsto para a próxima semana, poderá aumentar ainda mais a volatilidade.

"Não é um ambiente favorável para a Anthropic neste momento", afirmou Carsten Hesse, chefe da área de eventos relacionados a índices da Berenberg.

Anthropic mira US$ 90,4 bilhões na abertura de capital. — Foto: Arte/g1

articles.title: Juros e ajuste fiscal: o que está por trás da disparada do dólar? | G1
articles.standfirst: Moeda americana avançou 4% na semana e fechou a R$ 5,93, maior cotação desde abril de 2025.
articles.summary: Moeda americana alcançou o maior valor desde abril de 2025; fatores externos e incertezas sobre o ajuste fiscal pressionam o real.
articles.body:
Nas últimas semanas, o movimento de alta do dólar em todo o planeta tem pressionado com mais força o real. Por trás dessa alta, estão fatores globais e questões da economia brasileira.

A semana mais curta para o mercado encerrou antecipadamente o movimento de escalada da moeda americana. Foram só 4 dias de negociações, mas suficientes para uma forte alta.

O dólar começou a segunda-feira (16) negociado a R$5, 69. E fechou a quinta-feira (19), véspera do feriado, em R$5, 93. Alta de 4% em apenas uma semana.

É o maior valor desde 8 de abril de 2025, quando custava R$5,99.

Desde então, a moeda americana oscilou. Chegou a R$4,99 em maio deste ano e depois voltou a subir.

E os ventos mudaram completamente no fim de outubro, logo depois do segundo turno da eleição, quando a cotação disparou.

Uma tempestade formada por diferentes fatores, alguns deles, vindos de fora.

Quando cai o preço dos produtos que o Brasil vende para outros países, como o petróleo, pode entrar menos dólar no país.

A economia chinesa mais fraca também preocupa, porque a China é a principal compradora de produtos brasileiros.

E, com os juros altos nos Estados Unidos, investidores têm mais motivos para deixar o dinheiro por lá.

Com menos dólares circulando por aqui, a moeda americana fica mais cara.

"No caso dos Estados Unidos, nós já vimos uma alta das taxas de juros em setembro, e os principais diretores do Banco Central já avisaram que novas altas acontecerão, deverão ser algumas. Quando as taxas de juros nos Estados Unidos sobem, o que acontece? Os capitais, eles saem do resto do mundo e vão em direção à economia americana atrás desse rendimento mais, mais elevado. Isso torna a moeda americana mais forte em todo o mundo", explicou Marcelo Fonseca, economista-chefe da CVPAR.

Isso torna a moeda americana mais forte em todo mundo. Mas, entre os países emergentes, o real foi o que mais se desvalorizou nos últimos 30 dias.

"O mundo inteiro passa por uma volatilidade muito intensa, e o real tem sido influenciado também por esse movimento. É claro que aqui tem sido mais aguda em função das incertezas em relação à composição da Fazenda e do Planejamento, em relação ao controle e ao equilíbrio das contas públicas.", comentou André Galhardo, economista-chefe da Análise Econômica.

No Brasil, a expectativa dos investidores é pelo anúncio da nova equipe econômica do governo e da política fiscal para os próximos anos.

"Se o governo conseguir convencer as pessoas de que ele tem um plano de ajuste fiscal que é crível, é um plano de ajuste fiscal que ao longo do tempo, não precisa ser amanhã, mas ao longo do tempo ele coloque a trajetória da dívida pública em uma, em uma situação de estabilização, isso vai ajudar o trabalho do Banco Central. equacionamento da situação fiscal deverá em breve ajudar o Banco Central a, a voltar a cortar juros", disse Marcelo Fonseca, economista-chefe da CVPAR.

Real está entre as moedas que mais perderam valor diante do dólar — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Conmebol admite ter R$ 88 milhões aplicados no Ueno, banco paraguaio que quebrou após crise | G1
articles.standfirst: Entidade afirma que banco tinha boa classificação de risco quando os investimentos foram feitos e promete recorrer à Justiça para recuperar os recursos.
articles.summary: Entidade afirma que banco tinha boa classificação de risco quando os investimentos foram feitos e promete recorrer à Justiça para recuperar os recursos.
articles.body:
Vista aérea mostra a sede do Ueno Bank, em Assunção, no Paraguai. — Foto: Reuters

A Conmebol (Confederação Sul-Americana de Futebol) admitiu nesta sexta-feira (20) ter US$ 15 milhões (cerca de R$ 88 milhões ) aplicados no Ueno Bank, banco paraguaio que quebrou após uma crise financeira que provocou um escândalo político no país.

O Ueno foi liquidado pelo Banco Central do Paraguai no início de novembro. As perdas causadas pela quebra podem chegar a US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,8 bilhões) , segundo estimativas das autoridades paraguaias. (leia mais abaixo)

Em comunicado divulgado após uma reunião de seu conselho em Barranquilla, na Colômbia, a Conmebol informou que os recursos representam 1,8% de seus ativos totais.

A entidade afirmou que a situação não compromete suas atividades, mas anunciou que estuda medidas judiciais para recuperar integralmente o dinheiro.

"Essa situação desafortunada, que afeta parte do capital da instituição, não tem um impacto significativo nem compromete as operações atuais ou futuras da Confederação", afirmou.

A Conmebol também defendeu sua política de investimentos. Em comunicado, declarou que as aplicações são distribuídas entre instituições financeiras nacionais e estrangeiras, com “limites percentuais de exposição por instituição”, levando em conta a rentabilidade oferecida.

Atualmente, a Conmebol mantém investimentos em 32 bancos, no Paraguai e no exterior. A política da entidade permite aplicações apenas em instituições com classificação de risco na categoria A, indicativa de boa capacidade de honrar compromissos financeiros.

A confederação ressaltou que, quando os US$ 15 milhões foram investidos, o Ueno Bank atendia a essa exigência. "As decisões de investimento foram tomadas levando em consideração as condições e classificações de risco vigentes em cada momento", declarou.

"A instituição será firme e implacável na defesa de seus recursos e na promoção de todas as ações legais necessárias para sua recuperação, convencida de que cada dólar que pertence ao futebol sul-americano deve retornar ao futebol sul-americano", acrescentou.

O Ueno Bank, um dos maiores bancos do Paraguai, sofreu intervenção do Banco Central do país em 3 de novembro, após apresentar problemas de solvência . A medida deixou milhões de clientes temporariamente sem acesso às contas e desencadeou uma crise política no país.

Segundo o novo presidente do Banco Central paraguaio, Jorge Luis Schreiner, o colapso teve origem na concessão de empréstimos acima dos limites legais a empresas do próprio grupo econômico , além de vínculos entre executivos do banco e integrantes do poder político.

A crise culminou no impeachment e na prisão do então presidente Santiago Peña, suspeito de envolvimento no episódio , em meio a protestos populares. O ex-presidente do BC paraguaio, Carlos Carvallo, também foi detido, acusado de quebra de confiança e associação criminosa.

Em entrevista à agência France-Presse (AFP), divulgada nesta quinta-feira (19), Schreiner estimou que as perdas decorrentes da quebra podem chegar a US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 5,8 bilhões) , embora o valor definitivo ainda dependa da avaliação dos ativos da instituição.

"Não foi uma crise financeira, foi uma crise de um banco", afirmou o presidente do Banco Central.

O cálculo inclui cerca de US$ 700 milhões utilizados pelo Fundo de Garantia de Depósitos para ressarcir clientes , além de valores devidos a investidores que adquiriram títulos emitidos pelo banco no exterior.

De acordo com Schreiner, o BC conseguiu transferir as contas de aproximadamente 1,8 milhão de pessoas em menos de cinco dias após a intervenção. O ressarcimento dos depositantes respeita um limite equivalente a cerca de US$ 18 mil por cliente.

As autoridades também identificaram mais de US$ 1 bilhão em ativos do Ueno Bank, incluindo imóveis de alto valor, que poderão ajudar a cobrir parte das obrigações pendentes. Ainda não há, porém, uma estimativa definitiva de quanto poderá ser recuperado.

articles.title: Dez anos após Brexit, Reino Unido e UE negociam reaproximação  | G1
articles.standfirst: Novos acordos envolvem comércio, segurança e imigração; maioria dos britânicos hoje defende retorno ao bloco.
articles.summary: Rejeição à saída cresceu em meio às perdas econômicas, e Reino Unido começa a reconstruir relação com bloco europeu.
articles.body:
Dez anos depois de decidir sair da União Europeia, os britânicos sentem as perdas na economia, e começam buscar uma reintegração com o bloco europeu.

É uma reaproximação ainda tímida, mas histórica.

Reino Unido e União Europeia vão retomar a cooperação em áreas como segurança, imigração e, claro, comércio.

Um dos acordos vai diminuir o custo de exportação de alimentos e produtos agropecuários.

É um dos setores que mais sofreram desde o Brexit. E que ficou atolado em burocracias e filas - muitas filas - que desaceleram o comércio bilateral.

Andy Burnham - o atual primeiro-ministro britânico - diz que o divórcio foi um péssimo negócio.

Foi em junho de 2016 que os britânicos votaram pra sair da União Europeia.

O Brexit vendia a promessa de uma economia mais dinâmica. Com mais liberdade e dinheiro pra investir dentro do próprio país.

Nas ruas, teve protesto. Mas muita festa.

Só que hoje, dez anos depois, o clima está bem diferente. Se os britânicos tivessem que decidir agora se voltam ou não para União Europeia, a resposta seria: sim! 56% querem um retorno.

E se a pergunta fosse estreitar a relação com o bloco - em vez de uma adesão completa - o apoio seria ainda maior.

Nick Bloom é um economista britânico. Ele conta que não é uma tarefa fácil decifrar o impacto econômico do Brexit.

É que meses depois do divórcio, veio a pandemia. Teve ainda a guerra na Ucrânia, e agora no Irã. Com efeito direto no preço da energia.

Mas uma pesquisa do Nick e de outros economistas na Universidade de Stanford, nos Estados Unidos, mostra que o PIB per capita do Reino Unido está entre 6 e 8% menor por causa do Brexit.

"Nós comparamos o desempenho da economia britânica com o de outros 30 países desenvolvidos da Europa, América do Norte. E chegamos a esse gráfico aqui: repara que entre 2012 e 2016 - antes do Brexit - a média dessas economias estava bastante alinhada. Mas depois do referendo, o desempenho britânico começa a cair lentamente, e essa diferença vai ficando cada vez maior", explicou.

PIB per capita do Reino Unido está entre 6 e 8% menor por causa do Brexit. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Hoje, em 2026, qual o custo de estar fora da União Europeia? Um prejuízo de mais de R$ 30 mil - por ano, por pessoa, calcula Nick.

Andy Burnham disse que o acordo fechado hoje deve injetar 17 bilhões de libras no Reino Unido - e que os britânicos vão finalmente sentir um alívio no custo de vida.

O acordo também reabre as portas para que jovens estudem e até trabalhem dos dois lados da fronteira.

O presidente do Conselho Europeu, Antonio Costa, disse que o bloco está aberto a uma “relação o mais estreita possível” com o Reino Unido.

Depois do divórcio, seria esse um novo namoro?

Reino Unido e União Europeia negociam reaproximação — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO: Will the record listing stop the AI bubble from bursting
articles.summary: Five years after emerging as a startup founded by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic has made history with the biggest public stock offering ever.
articles.body: Five years after emerging as a startup founded by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic has made history with the biggest public stock offering ever. Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, around 34% above their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, before closing at $97.17, up 17.07%.The company raised $81.31 billion through the offering, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising haul. Its valuation briefly crossed $2 trillion during the first few minutes of trading before settling at around $1.75 trillion at the close.However, the strong debut did little to lift sentiment across the broader technology sector. US stocks came under pressure on Thursday, while Anthropic shares fell around 6% in premarket trading on Friday, slipping to $91.24.According to Reuters, the decline brought Anthropic's fully diluted valuation to around $1.7 trillion, while its market capitalisation based on shares outstanding stood at approximately $1.2 trillion.Anthropic's IPO is significant because it gives public market investors an opportunity to invest directly in an AI developer, rather than companies supplying the chips, computing infrastructure and data centres powering the technology."The reason that this IPO is so important is basically it's the first ability for the public investors to access a pure play AI trade," Fiona Cincotta from StoneX told BBC.She said previous offerings had largely involved other parts of the AI ecosystem, including semiconductor and data centre companies, while Anthropic's listing allows investors to access the AI provider itself.The offering is also expected to serve as a valuation benchmark for the wider AI industry. Its performance could influence investor sentiment towards other major players, including OpenAI, which has indicated that it could go public next year.Can the AI boom justify its valuations?Despite the strong demand, questions remain over whether AI companies can generate enough revenue to justify the enormous sums being invested in the technology.At an event last week, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon that his guiding principle was to "never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's worth".However, the economics of the AI boom remain contentious. Companies are spending heavily on chips, data centres, computing power and talent, with some AI employees commanding annual salaries exceeding $100 million.There are also concerns about revenue concentration. Around a quarter of Anthropic's revenue reportedly comes from a handful of companies, including Google and Amazon, while the US accounts for roughly two-thirds of its revenue.The industry also has a growing network of circular financing arrangements, with companies investing in AI developers while simultaneously supplying them with chips and computing infrastructure or buying their products."Anthropic’s IPO attracted strong investor demand, with the stock opening 34% above its IPO price and closing 17% higher. However, the broader AI and technology stocks came under pressure, highlighting that a successful listing does not automatically lift the wider sector. The broader market was already under strain, and investors are reassessing valuations and the amount of capital flowing into AI," Prateek Gupta, Head of Business at Mudrex, told TOI.""The listing also opens a new route for retail investors to access a company previously available largely through private markets. However, sustained performance will depend on business fundamentals and the ability to meet growth expectations. Investors should look beyond the initial rally and focus on valuation and long-term potential," Gupta added.Safety concerns and public backlashAnthropic was founded by seven former OpenAI employees, including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, over differences in their approach to AI development. The company sought to place greater emphasis on safety while building increasingly powerful AI systems.However, its rapid expansion has raised questions about whether its development pace matches its stated commitment to responsible AI.In an interview with CNBC, Amodei compared the rapid development of AI, partly driven by advanced models helping build improved versions of themselves, to allowing a driver to increase speed from 60 miles per hour to 200 miles per hour."What we've done with pacing is essentially said, 'Look, you know, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour, spend time figuring out how to do that safely,'" he said. "And the rest of that surplus, we spend building the model in the right way."He has also warned that AI could enable biological weapons development, mass surveillance and authoritarianism, while potentially displacing millions of white-collar workers.In its filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic devoted 93 pages to outlining potential business risks, including the possibility that advanced AI systems could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."The debate has also extended beyond the technology industry. Growing public opposition to data centres, concerns over energy and water consumption, and fears of job losses have made AI development an increasingly contentious political issue in the US.The next test for AI stocksDespite these concerns, investor enthusiasm remains strong. Orders for Anthropic shares reportedly exceeded the number available by more than six times, reflecting the fear of missing out on one of the biggest technology investment opportunities.However, a strong first-day performance does not necessarily guarantee long-term gains. SpaceX shares, for instance, initially rose nearly 70% from their IPO price of $135 to $225 before falling back to around $145, according to the figures cited in the BBC report.Some investors believe Anthropic's listing could reignite enthusiasm for AI stocks."Maybe the growth of the bubble has slowed down a little bit, but actually I wouldn't be willing to say that it's about to burst yet," Eileen Burbidge, founder of tech investor Passion Capital, told BBC. "I think this IPO could actually mean everyone could be off to the races again."Cincotta, meanwhile, believes the listing could have implications far beyond Anthropic, providing a benchmark for valuations across the AI industry.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Trump's tariff advantage for India is no favour: Why US cannot afford to lose New Delhi
articles.summary: Indians have always loved a good bargain, whether it is haggling over daily groceries or negotiating a trade deal with another country.
articles.body: Indians have always loved a good bargain, whether it is haggling over daily groceries or negotiating a trade deal with another country. After all, it is not a deal until you know you have secured better terms than the next person in line!After months of trade negotiations, the US has agreed to give India a comparative tariff advantage over peer economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact. However, the deal is yet to be signed.Earlier on Wednesday, India said it could sign the agreement only after the new tariff framework is in place and investigations under Section 301 are concluded.The India-US trade deal has seen several twists and turns since negotiations began in February 2025, from tariff threats and hopes of an agreement to a sudden courtroom setback. Now, with the deal back on the table, the latest development has raised a key question: What has changed, and why is the US suddenly offering the 'tariff king' a better deal?Until the framework of getting competitive advantage can be finalised, we can't enter into force a US deal...So that's broadly the discussions on how the US will find the appropriate tools and legal backing to give us that competitive advantage over our competitors.The two sides had finalised the first tranche of the pact, which proposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the US Supreme Court's decision to strike down the "reciprocal tariffs" put the agreement on hold.Now, Washington's willingness to give India a comparative tariff advantage over its peers has brought the negotiations back into focus.Why the US can't afford to lose the 'tough nut'India's importance to Washington goes well beyond trade figures. Its vast consumer market, supply of affordable medicines and potential to emerge as an alternative manufacturing base to China give the US several reasons to keep the partnership strong.Tariff competitiveness is another important part of the equation. When the first-phase BTA framework was finalised, India enjoyed a tariff advantage over ASEAN nations — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia — as well as Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh.But a lower tariff does not always mean a better deal.If India's rivals secure bigger tariff cuts, their products could become cheaper in the US market, leaving Indian exporters struggling to compete. The real advantage, therefore, lies not just in lower duties but in ensuring that India remains ahead of its competitors.So, what makes India a partner Washington cannot afford to overlook?Moving away from India might be a literal painIndia's importance to the US goes beyond trade, particularly when it comes to medicines. The country supplies 47% of US generic prescription drugs and 60% of hypertension medicines. Steep tariffs could hit American consumers and patients first.Rohit Kumar Singh of Eminence Strategy Consulting warns, “Disruption in supply might impact American citizens directly.”Replacing approved manufacturers, he adds, takes both investment and time.Even when the US threatened a 100% tariff on pharmaceutical imports, India remained largely shielded. Generics account for over 90% of medicines used in America and were exempted to avoid shortages and price spikes.Similarly, under the February 6 framework, the US had proposed scrapping reciprocal tariffs on Indian generics and their ingredients, with further concessions subject to a separate US investigation.India's $500 billion opportunity for US businessesThe proposed purchases under the interim trade framework also give American businesses a reason to support closer trade ties with India.Under an earlier statement, India had indicated its intention to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years. These included energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal.For perspective, India's imports from all countries stood at $527.21 billion during April-October 2026-27.Singh adds that pushing India too hard could jeopardise these potential sales.As Sandeep Gupta of Executive Access sums it up, “It’s a ‘we can scratch each other’s back effectively’ deal that works for both sides.”New Delhi even suggested to discuss tariffs first and postpone more difficult market access issues. The plan to purchase $500 billion worth of US products over five years gave American exporters an interest in the negotiations' result.US wants greater access to 140 crore buyersWith over 140 crore people, India is a shopper's paradise for American brands. Nearly 65% of Indians are under 35, and rising household incomes are expected to drive demand across categories, from appliances and cars to IT services. This creates opportunities for American companies selling technology, parts and financing.Geopolitics expert Jagvinder Singh Virk told TOI, “This young demographic, our expanding middle class, growing purchasing power and rapidly developing economy make India one of the most attractive markets in the world.”The US already sold India $45.4 billion worth of goods and $42.9 billion worth of services in 2025, according to USTR. Walking away from the partnership could mean losing access to an expanding market and future customers.Manufacturing and supply chainGlobal companies do not just want to sell in India; they also want to manufacture here and benefit from its growth.Virk says, “India is also emerging as a trusted global manufacturing and supply-chain partner.”Despite a bumpy global economic environment, India's exports grew over 16% in the first seven months of FY 2026-27.The US increasingly sees India as a strategic economic partner rather than just another trading destination. Its willingness to offer the country a tariff advantage over competing economies also reflects India's growing bargaining power in trade negotiations.Strategic partnershipIndia-US relations extend beyond trade, with both countries sharing strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.One example is the Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, which focuses on cooperation in maritime security and critical technologies. In May 2026, the four countries launched an Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance project and a framework to strengthen critical-mineral supply chains.Singh cautions that any weakening of this partnership “will make it harder to implement plans to develop alternatives to concentrated supply networks.”Ritik Bhandari, team lead, Centre for Law, Policy and Governance, NFPRC Foundation says that India's growing importance to the US is driven by both economic opportunities and shared strategic interests.He further points out that India offers Washington a large consumer base, manufacturing capabilities and scope for collaboration in technology and energy. Its role in diversifying global supply chains and strengthening the US presence in the Indo-Pacific further adds to its importance.The proposed tariff advantage, he says, reflects Washington's intention to ensure India remains competitive against other trading partners.India, a strategic counterweight to ChinaFor years, China has been America's factory floor, supplying everything from electronics to industrial components. But Washington is now looking to reduce that dependence, and India is emerging as an important alternative.Gupta said, “The US wants to reduce its dependence on China-dominated manufacturing items such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, minerals and manufacturing, which India can effectively offer.”US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer echoed this view in an interview with Fox News, acknowledging that “India can be a way station for that.”Losing India's trust, therefore, could prove costly for Washington on two fronts. American exporters risk losing access to Indian consumers, while US manufacturers could find themselves with fewer alternatives to Chinese suppliers.For the US, India is not just a trading partner but a crucial alternative for diversifying global supply chains and reducing overdependence on a few countries...America recognises India's importance, and any serious global economic strategy today must have India at its centre.India's approach: Firm on its terms, open to flexibilityIndia has made it clear that a trade deal cannot come at any cost. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had earlier said negotiations had reached a stage where further give-and-take would be “very, very difficult”, describing the pact as a “hard and very vigorously negotiated agreement”.Both countries, however, maintain that they are working towards a fair and mutually beneficial deal. US embassy deputy chief of mission Jason Meeks recently described the proposed partnership as “fair, reciprocal, and mutually beneficial”, with cooperation extending beyond goods.According to Jagvinder Singh Virk, India changed the tone of negotiations with “a clear economic vision, well-defined priorities and a willingness to find practical solutions”. New Delhi, he said, had shown that it could protect its core interests while remaining flexible where both sides stood to gain.Washington, too, has reasons not to push too hard. India offers US companies a vast consumer market, a young workforce, growing manufacturing capabilities and an opportunity to diversify supply chains.Comparing the talks with negotiations involving Canada and South Korea, Virk said India's growing economic strength and strategic importance set it apart.India, meanwhile, remains firm on sensitive sectors such as agriculture and dairy. It is open to a deal, but wants one that safeguards its interests and recognises its growing economic role.What's next for India?India-US ties may finally be turning a corner.Chief economic adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said recent weeks had shown signs of easing tensions, adding that a trade deal in early December could mean “we may have seen the worst of the unsettled phase behind us”.One of the bigger questions is whether the agreement can help India reduce its dependence on China. Initiatives such as Make in India, the PLI scheme and Aatmanirbhar Bharat offer a starting point. However, India must build its own manufacturing capabilities rather than simply replace dependence on China with dependence on the US.The next step, therefore, is to strengthen domestic capacity. Bhandari added that manufacturing incentives could encourage Indian companies to produce more raw materials at home, while long-term US orders could help fund these facilities."The government's focus on domestic manufacturing, infrastructure development and initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides a strong foundation for this transition. Importantly, India is approaching this partnership from a position of strategic autonomy, seeking to expand international economic cooperation while strengthening its domestic capabilities. This is an opportunity to reinforce India's economic resilience and global standing," Bhandari said.At the same time, India needs to find alternative sources for critical inputs. The real opportunity is not just to become an alternative to China, but to emerge as a manufacturing and technology powerhouse in its own right.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Gold price crash: From Rs 1.80 lakh to below Rs 1.25 lakh, will gold now plunge to Rs 1 lakh per 10 gms?
articles.summary: Gold is no longer glittery or shining - in fact gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year.
articles.body: Gold is no longer glittery or shining - in fact gold prices have crashed around 33% from the highs seen in India earlier this year. In 2025, there seemed no end in sight for gold’s spectacular rally. Come 2026, the year started with the yellow metal hitting a lifetime high of Rs 1.8 lakh per 10 grams in futures contract.And then the story went downhill - with no immediate bottom in sight!In the international markets, gold has dropped roughly 37% to around $3,527 per ounce, its lowest level in over a year. In India, MCX gold November futures recently slipped to around Rs 1,21,424 per 10 grams. The crash has been relatively less in India because the government hiked customs duty on gold and silver earlier this year, cushioning the fall to some extent.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Gold started falling in January as investors booked profit, but before it could find its equilibrium, the US-Iran war triggered another crash.Analysts say that the recent decline reflects a combination of profit-booking, liquidation of leveraged positions, changing interest-rate expectations and a stronger dollar.Key reasons for such a sharp fall include recent equity and tech-stock pullbacks, where investors sold liquid gold positions to raise cash or meet margin calls rather than using it as a shield while elevated bond yields and expectations of tighter interest rates in the US raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.So, is there an end in sight to this fall? What should investors do, and does the crash mean that gold has lost its safe haven appeal. We ask experts:Will gold fall to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams?Till a few weeks ago, a fall to Rs 1.25 lakh levels seemed unlikely, but that level too has been breached. So, does that mean that there is a chance of gold prices falling to Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams as well?Experts don’t rule out the possibility, though they believe that underlying fundamentals of gold such as central bank buying will continue to support the yellow metal. This indicates that a further fall may not sustain for long, they say.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says, “A decline towards Rs 1,00,000 cannot be ruled out if the rupee appreciates significantly and COMEX Gold corrects towards $3,000.”“However, the more important question is whether such lower levels can sustain and establish a long-term base. Given rapidly changing global investment themes and persistent geopolitical uncertainty, I do not expect prices to sustain below Rs 1,15,000 for long,” Trivedi tells TOI.Manav Modi, Commodities Analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd says, “The breach of Rs 1.25 lakh highlights how quickly sentiment and price expectations can change in a highly volatile market.”But, the analyst notes that a fall towards Rs 1 lakh would require a deeper strength in story as well positioning, potentially driven by sustained dollar strength, higher real yields, continued speculative unwinding and a moderation in investment demand.“However, the extent of the recent correction also needs to be assessed against gold’s underlying physical and central bank demand, which remains an important structural support,” he tells TOI.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma says that technically, the spot gold pair has extended a bearish phase following the recent breakdown below the previous consolidation phase.Moreover, the yellow metal holds well below the technically significant 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) validating the negative outlook.“While oversold technical indicators like RSI indicate that downside pace could slow but not yet reverse the trend. Having said that, a near term consolidation is still possible but could not stop the extension of a recent well established downtrend making gold vulnerable to fall further up to $3420-3380 / Oz in Spot (CMP $ 3575/Oz). On MCX futures, a sustainable close below Rs. 1,21,000/10 gm could accelerate its downtrend towards Rs. 1,18,000-1,16,000/10 gm on MCX,” he tells TOI.Has gold lost its safe haven status?No.Jateen Trivedi of LKP Securities believes that even though gold has witnessed a sharp correction, this does not mean it has lost its safe-haven status.“If we look at the two-year performance, prices have risen from around Rs 75,000 in January 2025 to nearly Rs 1,25,000 currently, delivering returns of approximately 55%,” Trivedi points out.“An asset that has preserved value for over 5,000 years will inevitably experience cycles of profit booking and corrections. Gold's safe-haven appeal remains intact; recent weakness reflects changing market dynamics rather than a loss of its investment relevance,” he adds.Commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma is of the view that gold’s long term role as a monetary and currency hedge still remains intact as long-term drivers like central bank buying and sovereign debt concerns remain relevant over time.But, Manav Modi cautions that while gold may not have lost its appeal as a safe haven asset, the recent price movements highlight that it is not immune to sharp corrections, particularly when speculative positioning becomes stretched.“Safe haven demand can also take a backseat when investors prioritise liquidity and reduce exposure across asset classes. Gold’s underlying role as a portfolio diversifier and reserve asset remains intact,” he tells TOI.Gold continues to be supported by central bank buying and recently ETF inflows. According to the latest World Gold Council report, Central bank buying jumped to 321t in Q3, eclipsing recent typical quarterly buying levels and lifting ytd demand to 675t. Gold ETFs reversed course following the Q2 outflows, adding 211t in Q3.So if the yellow metal continues to be a safe haven asset, what should your investment strategy in the current situation be?What should investors do and what’s the outlook for 2027?Experts believe the ongoing correction can be a good opportunity to accumulate gold, though cautiously and keeping your overall portfolio balance in mind.“This correction offers an opportunity to review gold allocation rather than panic over falling prices or focus on previous highs near Rs 1,80,000,” Jateen Trivedi says.“Investors should evaluate their overall portfolio allocation and consider staggered accumulation. Those with less than 15% allocation to gold may consider adding gradually, including a small lump-sum investment if significantly underinvested. The focus should be on long-term portfolio diversification rather than timing the exact bottom,” he recommends.Manav Modi recommends a staggered strategy to accumulate gold. “But, since further downside cannot be ignored, post some clarity, accumulation could be looked at,” he says.Finally, where is gold headed in 2027?Maneesh Sharma shares that a 20-25% recovery to around $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support which translates to a level of Rs 1,45,000-1,50,000/10 gm on MCX futures contract.Jateen Trivedi too believes that gold could move towards Rs 1,55,000-Rs 1,65,000 over the next year, depending on international prices and the rupee's trajectory.“COMEX Gold could potentially revisit the $4,500 zone, supported by central-bank demand and geopolitical uncertainty. However, continued rupee appreciation could limit domestic gains, resulting in Indian gold underperforming international prices,” he says.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Sebi proposes limiting tenure of chief executives, independent directors at exchanges
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Markets regulator Sebi on Friday proposed lowering the maximum age limit for public interest directors at stock exchanges and depositories to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Markets regulator Sebi on Friday proposed lowering the maximum age limit for public interest directors at stock exchanges and depositories to 70 years from 75, as part of a broader governance overhaul of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs).The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) also proposed tightening tenure limits for directors and top executives at these institutions, according to a consultation paper.Under the proposal, public interest directors would be allowed a maximum of two three-year terms, compared with three terms currently. Managing directors would be capped at two terms and eight years at a single MII, with an overall tenure limit of 12 years across such institutions.The regulator also proposed fresh tenure limits for executive directors. Existing heads would be allowed a maximum aggregate tenure of 15 years and could complete their ongoing terms.Sebi proposed extending restrictions on simultaneous directorships held by public interest directors to associates of MIIs. It also recommended reducing the number of statutory committees on which such directors can serve to four from five.The regulator said existing public interest directors and executive directors would be allowed to complete their current terms.Sebi has invited public comments on the proposals until December 11.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: How Claude propelled Anthropic start-up to become a $1.76 trillion giant in 5 years
articles.summary: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind chatbot Claude, has reached a valuation of roughly $1.76 trillion following its stock market
articles.body: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind chatbot Claude, has reached a valuation of roughly $1.76 trillion following its stock market debut on Nasdaq on Thursday. Founded just five years ago by former OpenAI employees, the company has made one of the fastest journeys from start-up to public listing, riding growing demand for AI technology and investor enthusiasm for the sector.The company's shares were priced at $83 each before trading began. They surged to $111.53 in the initial hours, taking its market value close to $2 trillion, before settling at $97.17 by the end of the session. The closing price represented a gain of roughly 17% over the allocation price.According to the BBC, Anthropic's listing is a crucial test for the AI industry, which has attracted enormous investment amid questions about whether the technology can justify the money being spent on it.From OpenAI employees to AI industry challengerAnthropic was founded five years ago by seven former OpenAI employees, led by siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei. The company has since become one of the prominent names in the AI industry, largely through its chatbot Claude.Its rise has coincided with major advances in computing power and related technology. These developments have made it possible to process far larger amounts of data and build AI chatbots that can simulate human conversations.Such tools can also perform tasks including software coding, digital image generation and internet searches. This has opened up new ways of using computers and fuelled demand for AI products.Anthropic's rapid journey from start-up to stock market listing reflects the growing interest in this technology. Its public debut also gives the company access to a wider pool of investors as it looks to finance its expansion.Why investors are watching AnthropicAnthropic's listing comes amid an unprecedented wave of spending on AI. More than $1 trillion was spent in the last year alone by a handful of major technology companies to build the infrastructure needed to develop and operate AI systems.The scale of investment has raised concerns about a possible financial bubble. The industry faces several challenges, including growing competition from cheaper AI models and shortages of expensive computer chips needed to run the technology.The US Federal Reserve has also flagged concerns about high AI-related debt being financed through "complex and opaque" structures. Its October meeting minutes also pointed to the concentration of AI exposure among a small number of companies.Anthropic's public listing could help it raise additional funds to meet the high costs of developing AI. Marta Norton, who heads strategy at investment firm Empower, told the BBC, "AI is financially demanding," adding that public markets open up access to more funding.A first for the AI industryAs the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic is entering a market where investors have few direct comparisons. Its shares could see significant fluctuations as the market assesses its prospects, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.The initial excitement around a public listing may not last, he said, pointing to the experience of Elon Musk-led SpaceX. Its shares rose about 10% on the first day of trading, taking its valuation to a record $2.2 trillion. However, they fell below their debut price within a month and have mostly declined further since.Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said: "There's no obvious peer to compare it to."Anthropic's co-founder and chief executive Dario Amodei has also been vocal about the risks posed by AI, including the possibility of a threat to human existence. The company has called for a slower pace of AI development and stronger safeguards, even as it pursues rapid growth.Reuters reported that Anthropic's market debut came as technology stocks faced pressure, with the Nasdaq Composite Index falling nearly 2.3% on Thursday. Alphabet shares dropped 2.9%, while Amazon lost almost 3.9%.The company's performance will now be closely watched as investors assess whether its growth prospects can justify its enormous valuation.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Water, power, noise: Anthropic's first Australia data centre faces major local opposition
articles.summary: Anthropic's first data centre project in Australia has faced overwhelming opposition from local residents, with 595 of nearly 600 public submissions
articles.body: Anthropic's first data centre project in Australia has faced overwhelming opposition from local residents, with 595 of nearly 600 public submissions either objecting to the development or seeking a delay over environmental concerns. The proposed Western Downs Digital Park, located about 250 km west of Brisbane, has Anthropic as its anchor tenant and is being developed by Zerra DC, news agency Reuters reported.Only two submissions supported the project, while one was neutral, according to a filing on the proposed development. The objections largely focused on concerns over water use, electricity demand, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.The proposed facility is planned on farmland, away from suburban areas. However, its planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would make it one of Australia's biggest data centres. About one-third of the submissions came from people living within 200 km of the site, the filing said.A Zerra spokesperson said the developer took the submissions seriously, adding that they "reinforce that people want a greater say in how the project develops".The company said it was expanding its community engagement and planned to report on changes sought by the public. Anthropic declined to comment.The timeline of submissions also showed a rise in opposition after Anthropic was named as the project's tenant on September 15. The project had received five objections in a month before the announcement, while the remaining submissions came in between September 15 and November 11, when the local government stopped accepting them.The opposition comes amid growing concerns among communities about the rapid expansion of data centres, often described as AI factories, around the world. The boom in data centre infrastructure has been valued at $7 trillion by 2030 by McKinsey.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: China bars new red-chip firms from offshore listings without shifting base
articles.summary: China's securities regulator has told law firms that it will not approve overseas listing plans by red-chip companies set up after March 2023 unless they
articles.body: China's securities regulator has told law firms that it will not approve overseas listing plans by red-chip companies set up after March 2023 unless they shift their domicile to mainland China, people familiar with the matter said. The move tightens Beijing's oversight of offshore fundraising and could affect Chinese companies planning to list in Hong Kong and New York.The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) conveyed the guidance to law firm representatives in recent days, the people said. They declined to be identified because the regulatory discussions were confidential, news agency Reuters reported.Red-chip companies are incorporated overseas, often in tax havens, but control businesses and assets in China through equity ownership or contractual arrangements. The structure has been popular among Chinese startups, particularly technology firms, seeking access to foreign investors and deeper capital markets.China's oversight of red-chip companies has gradually increased. Before March 2023, Chinese firms using overseas holding structures to raise funds abroad did not require regulatory approval.That changed with the introduction of new offshore listing rules in March 2023. In March this year, the CSRC told Reuters it was examining the "necessity and compliance" of red-chip structures, particularly those established after the rules came into effect.Despite the warning, some companies planning IPOs and their advisers continued to seek approval for overseas listings without dismantling their existing structures or shifting their domicile to China, one of the people said.Most failed to convince the regulator that retaining a red-chip structure was necessary, prompting the tougher stance, the person added.The move comes as China and the US compete for an edge in technology, particularly in artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Chinese authorities have stepped up scrutiny of technology, data and capital flowing outside the country.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: 'Pee on your brain, rip your heart out': How Jensen Huang 'tortured' employees repeatedly
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang repeatedly humiliated and threatened employees during his tenure at the chipmaker, using violent language and public
articles.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang repeatedly humiliated and threatened employees during his tenure at the chipmaker, using violent language and public put-downs as part of his management style, a New York Times report said on Friday. The report, citing current and former employees, detailed incidents spanning nearly two decades, including threats to physically harm subordinates and insults directed at them during company meetings.Huang had spoken about his approach to management during a fireside chat two years ago. “I’d rather torture you into greatness because I believe in you,” he said.The accounts offer details of the management culture at Nvidia, which Huang transformed from a graphics-chip business into a major player in the artificial intelligence industry over 33 years.Public humiliation and threats at workplaceAccording to the report, Huang regularly reprimanded managers in front of their teams. In one instance, he went around a room and told managers he would kill them, a person familiar with the incident told the New York Times.When he reached an employee in their 70s, Huang reportedly said the person was very old and that everyone was hoping they would drop dead.Huang allegedly told one employee that their mother should have "aborted" them and threatened another that he would rip off their head and “pee on your brain”. In another incident, he reportedly told a subordinate he would rip both their arms off and beat them to death with them.In a separate incident, Huang allegedly threw a water bottle at an executive during a fit of anger. He also reportedly told Jay Puri, Nvidia's then-executive vice-president of worldwide field operations: “I hope you get the flu and I hope it gets worse,” and “I hope you die and put us all out of our misery.”Complaints over management style date back to 2005The report traced complaints about Huang's behaviour to at least the mid-2000s. Michael Winston, a former senior vice-president of human resources, threatened legal action against Nvidia in 2005 after alleging he was fired for objecting to Huang's conduct.During a two-day off-site meeting attended by around 50 employees, Huang allegedly made violent threats. “You have to do this, or I will rip your f–king heart out and stomp on it,” he reportedly said.Winston wrote in notes at the time that Huang “thinks he can get away with anything” and that employees were “terrorized” and asking him to intervene.Winston said he confronted Huang and warned him that his behaviour had “crossed the line” and could expose the company to lawsuits. Huang allegedly described the treatment as a “rite of passage” for employees and added: “It has good entertainment value,” according to the report.Winston was fired that November. Huang reportedly told him he was “not a good fit” and threatened to ensure he would never work again if he sued the company.Winston later filed a formal complaint with California's Department of Fair Employment and Housing and drafted a lawsuit. He reached a confidential settlement with Nvidia for $1 million before the lawsuit was filed. Winston died earlier this year.Employees divided over Huang's leadershipSix current and former employees told the New York Times that Huang's management style had created a workplace culture they compared to Stockholm syndrome, in which hostages develop an emotional bond with their abusers.As Nvidia grew and its employees became wealthy, Huang reportedly told groups of subordinates that money alone was no longer enough to motivate them and that he needed to humiliate them.The report also said some executives adopted similar behaviour. Huang's daughter, Madison Huang, who works in marketing at Nvidia and effectively served as his de facto chief of staff, reportedly used terms such as “dead-face” for employees who remained expressionless after being reprimanded in meetings. She also allegedly called employees “goldfish” if they could not remember something, according to the Wall Street Journal.Despite the accounts of his management style, Huang retained support among many employees. More than 200,000 people have signed an online petition calling for his reinstatement as CEO.Nvidia's board has not supported the idea. Interim CEO Colette Kress, who was herself reportedly belittled by Huang during a company meeting, urged employees to “move forward” during the first all-hands meeting held without him, according to sources cited in the report.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: US stocks slide as AI sell-off intensifies; S&P 500 approaches correction
articles.summary: Wall Street's sell-off deepened on Friday as a sharp decline in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks dragged the S&P 500 close to correction territory and
articles.body: Wall Street's sell-off deepened on Friday as a sharp decline in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks dragged the S&P 500 close to correction territory and put the benchmark index on course for its biggest weekly loss in months.The S&P 500 fell around 2%, leaving it about 10% below its record high of October 6. A closing decline of more than 10% from that peak would put the index in what investors call a “correction”. The index was also on track to post its seventh consecutive day of losses, its longest losing streak since the start of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020.The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slid 3.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 289 points, or 0.6%, as of 12:20 pm Eastern time.Despite gains in a larger number of S&P 500 stocks, losses among major technology companies weighed heavily on the index because of their large market valuations. AI-linked stocks, which had driven much of Wall Street's gains this year, were now leading the decline.Investors have grown concerned that the high valuations of AI companies may not be justified by their earnings prospects and that their heavy spending on the technology could take time to generate returns. Fears of a bubble in the sector have added to the pressure.The sell-off also comes amid a shift in political power following the midterm elections, in which the Republican Party, widely seen as more supportive of the technology industry, suffered an electoral setback.Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI chatbot, also came under pressure in its market debut. Its shares fell 12.4% to $85.16 on Friday, although they remained above the initial public offering (IPO) price of $83.The company's listing was the biggest public stock offering on record, with its valuation briefly crossing $2 trillion. However, its shares joined the broader technology sell-off on Friday.Newly listed technology companies often see sharp price swings in the days following their market debut. SpaceX, which previously held the record for the biggest IPO, gained nearly 50% in its first three trading days before falling below its IPO price a month later.Chipmakers, which have benefited from rising investment in AI data centres, were among the biggest losers, the Associated Press reported.Nvidia fell 7.4%, marking its ninth decline in the past 10 trading sessions. The company also faced pressure amid concerns about its future following the reported sudden downfall of its former CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang.Advanced Micro Devices dropped 11.7%, while Broadcom declined 11.5%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index slid 9%.Outside the technology sector, however, several stocks advanced. General Mills, the maker of Cheerios, rose 4.8%, while homebuilder Lennar gained 3.4%.In the bond market, US Treasury yields fell. The yield on the 10-year Treasury slipped to 4.93% from 5.04% late on Thursday.Brent crude, the international benchmark, declined 0.3% to $91.69 a barrel despite continuing tensions near the Strait of Hormuz amid the US war with Iran.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: FCC grants tech import waivers as firms boost US investment
articles.summary: By David Shepardson WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The Federal Communications Commission said on Friday it has granted approvals to 71 companies in 2026 to c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The Federal Communications Commission said on Friday it has granted approvals to 71 companies in 2026 to continue importing drones, ‌wireless routers, robots and power inverters that would have been barred under US ‌national security restrictions.

The US telecommunications regulator is trying to push Chinese gear out of technology supply chains and ​spur domestic manufacturing.

The FCC said the companies that have won approvals have agreed to invest $4.4 billion and create 4,700 jobs to move tech equipment production as a condition of approval for the waivers. The so-called Covered List has been used by the FCC to ban tech equipment on ‌national security grounds and has ⁠been one of the most significant parts of the Trump administration's China policy.

"The FCC's Covered List has proven to be an essential tool in ⁠our national security toolkit, protecting America's networks and communications infrastructure from dangerous products," said FCC Chair Brendan Carr, a Republican, adding that it has "also generated a surge in investment in American manufacturing."

The ​Covered List ​has been used by the FCC to ban ​new Chinese drones, robots, routers and ‌power inverters. Reuters has reported that the FCC could use the list to ban imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers that are crucial to data centers.

FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, a Democrat, on Thursday questioned how the list has been used.

"Its original purpose was to keep insecure equipment out of our networks, and that is targeted towards adversary countries," ‌Gomez said. She added that the Trump administration has ​used the Covered List for items with ties to ​telecom or IT equipment "to gain concessions ​that have nothing to do with security" and that it has "instead become ‌an industrial policy tool."

In September, the Republican ​chair of the US ​House of Representatives Energy and Commerce Committee and the panel's top Democrat proposed overhauling use of the Covered List.

The proposed legislation signaled congressional concern about how the FCC ​is using its authority to ‌restrict Chinese technology and would require the agency to seek input from other ​government agencies before determining whether foreign technology poses an unacceptable national security ​risk.

articles.title: Trump critiques Jensen Huang's replacement as he wades deeper into Nvidia turmoil
articles.summary: President Trump on Friday offered a defense of ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, but — perhaps more significantly — criticized the new leadership of the chipma...
articles.body:
President Trump on Friday offered a defense of ousted Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, but — perhaps more significantly — criticized the new leadership of the chipmaker.

The comments came during a press conference in which the president again praised Huang's role in developing the company's advanced Blackwell chips.

"Jensen did that, and I think there are very few people in that company that can do that," the president said.

"I'm not trying to be disrespectful," Trump added of Huang's replacements. "I watched the people talking about how the company's going to be and where it's going to be." He didn't finish the thought, other than to say of Huang, "I would love to see him be back."

It was a clear reference to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress and new board chair Harvey Jones, who took over last week following Huang's resignation and faced some criticism for their presentation on the company's earnings call earlier this week.

Kress took the reins of the company after Huang built close ties with the Trump administration. Huang was often seen in Washington at Trump's side or traveling with the president. He accompanied Trump to China earlier this year.

Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a direct subordinate amid questions about whether he oversaw the evasion of US export controls on advanced semiconductor chips.

Trump has noted Huang's desire to sell chips in China, but said he wants "only older chips" to be available.

"I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump said on Friday. "We're a country of second chances."

Trump also showed support for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Friday, saying "I have not lost confidence" in his Cabinet member, whom he called "a different kind of a guy."

"He has a natural business instinct. I think he's done a very good job," Trump said.

Lutnick has been under fire for suggestions that he moved too slowly on the Trump administration's push to crack down on advanced chips from Nvidia and others making their way into Chinese hands.

Tom Cotton of Arkansas, a top Republican senator, told the Wall Street Journal Friday that Lutnick had repeatedly ignored warnings that US chips were being smuggled into China.

Cotton stopped short of saying Lutnick should be fired but declined to support him.

Both Lutnick and Huang are set to testify publicly before lawmakers in the weeks ahead in what could be two of Washington's most closely watched congressional grillings in years.

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Goldman Says Stock Selloff Has Legs as Panic Index Nears Maximum
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s panic gauge climbed near its maximum level as US stocks tumbled Friday, signaling that another substantial wave of selling will fo...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc.'s panic gauge climbed near its maximum level as US stocks tumbled Friday, signaling that another substantial wave of selling will follow over the coming week, according to the bank's traders.

Goldman's trading desk said the selloff has spread across the so-called systematic investors, as the bank's Panic Index rose to 9 out of 10. Momentum traders, such as commodity trading advisers, sold $57 billion in equities over the past month, with their net positioning in US stocks turning short by $19 billion, according to Goldman estimates.

The bank's models are projecting that CTAs could offload another $65.8 billion in a flat market, $28.6 billion if stocks rise and as much as $80.6 billion if equities continue to decline.

The market's latest leg lower reflects growing investor reluctance to buy the dip in technology stocks, even as Anthropic PBC's blockbuster initial public offering was seen as a potential catalyst for a broader recovery in risk appetite. Instead, the listing has failed to deliver the anticipated market-wide boost.

Many investors were looking for the world's biggest offering "to act as a clearing event to usher a 'risk-back-on' trade into year end," Goldman traders wrote in a note. "Without this force it has been a tough pill to swallow."

The selling threatens to reinforce an already difficult market environment, as falling prices trigger further reductions in exposure by trend-following strategies, which adjust their positions based on the stock market direction and volatility.

Investors are increasingly questioning whether the enormous spending on AI infrastructure, chips and computing capacity will generate returns sufficient to justify the valuations across the sector. The concerns were compounded by the turmoil at Nvidia Corp., which led to the ouster of chief executive Jensen Huang.

Crowded positions and momentum-driven strategies have exacerbated volatility, with technology shares at the center of the selloff. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% Friday in its worst week since March 2020 and the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index tumbled 11%, dragged by losses in Nvidia, which has plunged nearly 50% from its Oct. 6 peak after a 14% slump Friday.

articles.title: VIX Hits Highest Level Since 2025 Tariff Turmoil as Volatility Warning Signs Flash
articles.summary: The stock market’s main volatility gauge jumped to its highest level since April 2025 as the S&P 500 capped its worst week in seven months.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The stock market's main volatility gauge jumped to its highest level since April 2025 as the S&P 500 capped its worst week in seven months.

The Cboe Volatility Index, better known as the VIX, touched 40 late in the session as stocks extended their slide late in the day, the highest level for the gauge of expected S&P 500 price swings since the tariff turmoil. But while traders are having to pay up for option contracts to protect against bigger swings, there's little sign of panic in the broader market.

The rise in the VIX was more of a mechanical response to the 3.6% fall in the S&P 500 than because of a desperate rush to buy more protection, according to Mandy Xu, head of derivatives market intelligence at the Cboe Global Markets Inc., which created the gauge. "There's a lot more uncertainty in the near term, but not necessarily a lot more fear."

She said that more than four-fifths of the move was due to the drop in the S&P 500 and the knock-on effect that had on the pricing of longer-dated options, rather than because of demand for downside protection.

While the VIX moving into the 30s is a signal of market stress, such events typically happen several times a year, and rarely for more than a few days at a time.

Still, some investors are betting that volatility will persist.

"Conditions may be ripe for a big right tail move in the VIX," Matthew Thompson, managing partner at Thompson Capital Management, said in a call around noon New York time on Friday. The VIX added nine more points on Friday afternoon to briefly touch 40.

The firm is now long index volatility using VIX futures contracts.

articles.title: 'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
articles.summary: By Lewis Krauskopf NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) -  Investors next week will focus on consumer spending, looking for evidence that a broadly solid economy can h...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors next week will focus on consumer spending, looking for evidence that a broadly solid economy can help calm a US stock market unsettled by doubts about the AI trade.

The S&P 500 and the Dow tumbled on Friday, confirming they were in a correction, while Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut that had ‌raised hopes of easing worries about an AI trade already roiled by valuation concerns.

Next week, "Black Friday" heralds the onrush of the holiday shopping season as retailers offer a wave of discounts. ‌Investors will watch for signs of how consumers are coping with inflation, including rising energy and borrowing costs. Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

"If you continue to see a strong consumer, it should help to lift the economy," said Jim ​Baird, chief investment officer with Plante Moran Financial Advisors. "That directly contributes back to stronger corporate revenue and earnings growth, and provides a catalyst for investors that extends beyond the AI trade and to other parts of the economy."

Investors are still digesting a steep pullback in heavyweight technology and AI stocks.

This week, the blockbuster market debut from Claude creator Anthropic and a solid quarterly report from beleaguered AI chipmaker Nvidia failed to steady the stock market. Spurred by concerns about heavy financing needs and political pushback, doubts have emerged about the massive spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure that has underpinned the 4-year-old bull market.

"Markets and investors are looking at the tech sector ‌with a lot more questions," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and ⁠market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management.

The Anthropic IPO offered investors their first chance to invest in a publicly traded AI lab, and the stock's performance was expected to drive broad sentiment in coming days. Anthropic's shares opened sharply higher on their first day of trading, then pared gains and closed up 17% on Thursday, while ⁠major stock indexes sank. On Friday, Anthropic fell 9%.

The S&P 500 has fallen 11.6% from its October 6 all-time high, dragged down by the technology sector, which has slumped nearly 24.7% in that time.

A recent series of technology snafus that disrupted areas from banking to travel to email also left investors edgy heading into a US trading week that will be shortened due to the Thanksgiving holiday.
