articles.title: US market regulator probes issues in Nvidia's accounting practices: Report
articles.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, with enforcement staff scrutinising potential accounting
articles.body: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, with enforcement staff scrutinising potential accounting issues at the chipmaker, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters. The probe adds to mounting pressure on the company, which is already facing scrutiny over its business links to a Singapore-based firm investigated for suspected shipments of AI chips to China.The investigation, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, is focused on potential accounting issues, the two people said. The probe comes amid renewed scrutiny of Nvidia's accounting disclosures, particularly its reporting of revenue from Singapore.Last year, Nvidia changed its method of reporting geographic revenue, using customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses. The company said the change would provide a more accurate picture of its revenue distribution, but Singapore was subsequently removed from its geographical breakdown.The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported this week that Nvidia made the change even as sales in Singapore had surged to almost half of its global revenue.The issue has drawn attention amid investigations into possible shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China through Southeast Asia, which has emerged as a hub for suspected chip-smuggling activity following US export restrictions.US authorities have been investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed since 2024 over possible export-control violations involving alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week. Megaspeed was historically a large Nvidia customer and was led by Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied the allegation. The company has said Alice Huang left in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business".The SEC's inquiry comes as investors raise questions about complex financing arrangements across the AI industry. Nvidia has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees linked to data-centre projects using its equipment.Critics say such arrangements could make it harder for investors to assess the quality of reported revenue and companies' financial exposure. SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock told Reuters last month that the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure investors receive a full picture of potential risks.On Tuesday's earnings call, Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company would be more selective about financing deals across the AI industry.Mounting legal and regulatory pressureThe accounting probe is the latest challenge for Nvidia, whose shares have been hit by a wider scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, alongside the investigation into Megaspeed.The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion proposed acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face as part of a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and business practices, Reuters reported last month.Nvidia shares fell about 13 per cent on Friday after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe, extending losses from an earlier decline of more than 6%.The SEC under President Donald Trump has said it will focus on traditional securities violations, including accounting fraud. It recently created a financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division to develop cases involving accounting and auditing practices.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown
articles.summary: Washington has new rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips, but lawmakers want more.
articles.body:
United States lawmakers say more regulations are needed to protect advanced AI chips once they leave the country, even as they support the recently imposed chip export controls.

This week, the US Department of Commerce announced a new rule to restrict how advanced US AI chips can be accessed remotely in the wake of the previous Nvidia CEO’s affair with a suspected spy for Beijing. The move would close what officials described as a loophole that allows Chinese companies to tap into computing power through data centres in third countries, bypassing US restrictions.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which sits under the Commerce Department, said the rule would require data centre customers in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Brazil to apply for a special licence to buy advanced chips from US companies, including Nvidia, because they “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.

“The export controls should have been in place, certainly,” Democratic Representative Pramila Jayapal told Al Jazeera. “I also think it’s a bigger conversation about who dominates the AI market. We should not have this consolidation of all the AI knowledge in a couple of companies because that poses an enormous threat on multiple levels, including national security.”

In October, Jayapal introduced a policy framework that would require every AI company operating in the US to obtain a federal charter in an effort to protect the public interest.

The AI charter, the framework says, is modelled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons.

The framework also bans AI companies from building empires, releasing risky models, stealing through surveillance, exploiting workers, or causing harm.

Jayapal is a member of the House of Representatives Judiciary Committee, whose ranking members announced a probe to determine whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had blocked efforts to stop the suspected smuggling of advanced Nvidia chips to China.

Lutnick is facing criticism, including from members of US President Donald Trump’s cabinet, for allegedly refusing to impose restrictions on companies accused of diverting advanced chips to China, including Megaspeed, which is at the centre of the Nvidia probe.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee also announced that the Trump administration had approved exports of 879,000 chips manufactured by Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026.

Democrats, who will control both chambers of Congress in January, expressed a desire to better limit chip exports amid growing scrutiny over the extent to which US computing power may have reached China.

“I’m excited to get these gavels and go through the investigatory work that’s necessary, but also to rein in and regulate artificial intelligence. The very industry is asking to be regulated by Congress,” Democratic Representative Everton Blair told Al Jazeera.

The US accounts for nearly 75 percent of the world’s AI spending and computing power, followed by China.

US tech giants, including Amazon, Microsoft and Google, operate nearly 90 major AI computing hubs globally, according to an Oxford University study. The same research found that US companies were building 63 AI computing hubs outside the country as of 2025.

Stephen Ezell, vice president for global innovation policy at the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF), said Washington would find it difficult to enforce the BIS rule.

China has rejected the restriction, calling it “economic coercion” by the US.

On Friday, after his return to the White House from his historic trilateral meeting with the Chinese and Russian presidents in Shenzhen, China, Trump promised to prohibit US companies from developing data centres in other countries.

“We’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it,” Trump said.

It was unclear what Trump had envisioned, or how he would enforce it.

At the same time, he urged Americans to embrace data centres in their neighbourhoods, despite communities’ increasing concern about the centres’ impact on quality of life, environment and energy demands.

Analysts say the recent export regulation has likely not had much effect on China’s efforts to become the global leader in AI semiconductor chips.

“China does not want to depend upon American or other foreign semiconductors. They want to develop them themselves, and one can argue that we’ve slowed them down a little bit with our export controls, but in no way has it changed China’s aspirations to become the global AI semiconductor chip leader,” Ezell said on Al Jazeera’s This Is America .

articles.title: Trump again urges Fed to lower interest rates
articles.summary: Presented by Bitget. {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Trump again urges Fed to lower interest rates President Trump on Friday reiterated his view that the Federal Reserve should lower interest rates, as officials are likely to hike borrowing costs at their meeting in early December. © Jacquelyn Martin, Associated Press…
articles.body:
Trump again urges Fed to lower interest rates

President Trump on Friday reiterated his view that the Federal Reserve should lower interest rates , as officials are likely to hike borrowing costs at their meeting in early December.

“Interest rates are too high, because we have a very political Fed ,” the president told reporters in the White House press briefing room.

Trump has repeatedly urged the central bank to lower rates, arguing it will lead to higher economic growth for the country. He often blasted former Fed Chair Jerome Powell during his first year back in office for not backing rate cuts earlier.

This time around, the president stressed he was “not blaming” Kevin Warsh , his hand-picked successor to Powell, for the Fed raising interest rates by a quarter point in September.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) hiked rates to contain stubborn inflation , which has remained above the Fed’s 2 percent target for five and a half years.

Officials held rates steady last month, keeping them at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent .

But as elevated inflation persists and multiple Fed officials signal future rate hikes, traders are pricing in a 91.5 percent chance of the FOMC raising rates by a quarter point at its next gathering on Dec. 8-9, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Trump laid out the counterargument on Friday, saying the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) would be “15 or 20” percent with lower interest rates. The nation’s GDP grew at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter, the Bureau of Economic Analysis reported last month.

“When we have these great numbers that we have, you shouldn’t keep raising rates, you should lower rates,” the president told reporters.

Trump later said, “We should have the lowest interest rate anywhere in the world , because we’re the one, we’re the country that makes other countries successful.”

articles.body: MUMBAI: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) Friday unanimously approved a Rs 50-crore grant to the charitable trust that runs Pune's Jehangir Hospital, but only after trustees discussed whether the funding presented a potential conflict of interest as hospital chairman Jehangir H C Jehangir is one of only 3 permanent trustees of closely linked Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT). articles.title: Historic Winner of Texas Oil Regulator Seat Wants Faster Permits
articles.summary: The first Democrat in 36 years to win a seat on the commission that governs the oil and gas industry in Texas said he plans to work with his Republican colle...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The first Democrat in 36 years to win a seat on the commission that governs the oil and gas industry in Texas said he plans to work with his Republican colleagues to speed up permitting in the state.

Texas Railroad Commission member-elect Jon Rosenthal said he aims to find ways to incentivize the industry to expand "responsibly" and did not express plans to reduce oil production in the state.

"We should be partnering with folks in the industry because they're the ones who understand this intimately," Rosenthal said Friday in an interview with Bloomberg. "I've talked to folks out there in the real world who have been working on this permit or that permit for months or even years. They're way behind."

The three-member commission is responsible for overseeing the $200 billion Texas oil and gas industry. Its purview expanded from managing freight rates more than 100 years ago to handling drilling permits and well inspections as well as enforcing safety and pollution rules. The agency provided the template for OPEC's founders in 1960.

Rosenthal defeated Republican firebrand Bo French on Nov. 3 amid a so-called blue wave that saw Texas Democrats sweep the governor's office, a US senate seat and a host of down-ballot races in the state.

A self-described "drill-baby-drill Democrat," Rosenthal is no stranger to the energy industry. He worked for 25 years as a mechanical engineer for some of the world's biggest oil field contractors, including SLB and NOV Inc. Rosenthal is also familiar with the state legislature as he's wrapping up a fourth term as a state representative from the Houston area. One of his main priorities is beefing up the commission's ranks.

"I am going to strongly advocate for increased funding, not just for ramping up well plugging, which clearly needs to happen, but also to hire some more folks at the agency to raise their pay scale so that we can be more competitive," said Rosenthal, who served on the legislature's Energy Resources Committee, which oversees the Railroad Commission. "There's some new leadership that my existing relationships I think will be helpful to our effort as a commission."

Since the US midterms, Rosenthal said he's met with Railroad Commission Chair Christi Craddick as well as outgoing Commissioner Jim Wright, a Republican who lost to French in the primary. Rosenthal said he plans to meet with the other sitting commissioner, Wayne Christian, in about a week.

articles.title: US judge rejects CFTC emergency bid to block New York from policing Kalshi
articles.summary: By Jonathan Stempel NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - A federal judge rejected on Friday the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's request to temporarily bloc...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - A federal judge rejected on Friday the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's request ‌to temporarily block New York Attorney General Letitia James from ‌pursuing an enforcement case against prediction markets operator Kalshi.

US District Judge Lorna Schofield in Manhattan ​said the CFTC had "not established a likelihood of success on the merits" of its argument that federal law preempted states from enforcing their own gambling laws against prediction markets operators, including requirements that operators obtain gaming ‌licenses.

The CFTC did not ⁠immediately respond to a request for comment.

Schofield noted that three federal appeals courts have ruled that states could ⁠regulate Kalshi, while a fourth said New Jersey could not.

That split increases the likelihood that the US Supreme Court will eventually decide the issue.

Schofield ruled ​one ​day after US District Judge Vernon Broderick ​in Manhattan granted New York's ‌request to move its lawsuit against Kalshi back to the Manhattan state court where it was filed on July 31.

That prompted the CFTC to make what it called an emergency request for a late-afternoon hearing to temporarily halt New York's enforcement activity.

The regulator said moving the case ‌left "no practical barrier to New York moving ​full steam ahead" against Kalshi.

James alleged that Kalshi ​should have obtained a New York ​State Gaming Commission license to operate its platform, ‌where people trade on the predicted ​outcomes of sports, ​elections and other events.

She said such platforms can encourage problem gambling and endanger people's financial, emotional and physical health.

The CFTC regards Kalshi's ​contracts as "swaps" and ‌has sued 12 states to defend what it calls its ​exclusive jurisdiction over US derivatives markets.

(Reporting by Jonathan Stempel in ​New York; Editing by Sanjeev Miglani)

articles.title: Casten, Lieu propose whistleblower program for prediction market insider trading
articles.summary: Reps. Sean Casten (D-Ill.) and Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) introduced new legislation Friday to regulate prediction markets and prevent insider trading, allowing whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing. The Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act would create a program at the Justice Department for people with knowledge of insider trading to come forward and…
articles.body:
Reps. Sean Casten (D-Ill.) and Ted Lieu (D-Calif.) introduced new legislation Friday to regulate prediction markets and prevent insider trading, allowing whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing.

The Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act would create a program at the Justice Department for people with knowledge of insider trading to come forward and potentially receive financial compensation for information leading to successful enforcement.

“Prediction markets have a serious insider trading problem,” Casten said. “By encouraging whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing, we can take an important step in cracking down on insider trading to restore accountability and public confidence in the U.S. rule of law.”

Improper use of betting markets has been in the spotlight multiple times this year, among political candidates, service members and even White House staff.

In August, President Trump’s teleprompter operator was placed on leave and investigated for placing bets on the content of the president’s speeches before they were made public. Later that month, a Republican congressional candidate in North Carolina was suspended from Kalshi for betting on her own race. Kalshi had previously suspended three other congressional candidates in April.

Other examples of misuse include a U.S. Army soldier betting on the U.S. operation in Venezuela and nine accounts on Polymarket making $2.4 million on bets about military action in Iran. House Oversight and Government Reform Committee Chair Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) announced an investigation into Kalshi and Polymarket in May.

In a statement about the bill Friday, Lieu cited some of the examples as a reason for legislative action.

“Government insiders should not be able to profit from betting on U.S. military operations or the contents of a President’s speech. They should not be able to use their positions of public trust to manipulate prediction markets,” Lieu said.

Kalshi recently said it had eliminated the option to place bets on Trump’s comments in response to a Commodity Futures Trading Commission order, having previously argued that Trump-mention markets “present a heightened risk of manipulation.”

With Republicans still in the majority, Casten and Lieu’s bill will need bipartisan support to pass before the end of the year, though it could be reintroduced once the new Congress — with a sizable Democratic majority — is sworn in.

articles.title: AI sell-off batters Wall Street; S&P 500 enters correction, Nasdaq turns negative for year
articles.summary: Wall Street stocks tumbled on Friday as a sharp sell-off in technology and artificial intelligence-related shares intensified, pushing the Nasdaq
articles.body: Wall Street stocks tumbled on Friday as a sharp sell-off in technology and artificial intelligence-related shares intensified, pushing the Nasdaq Composite into negative territory for the year and sending the S&P 500 into correction territory.The S&P 500 plunged 3.7 per cent to 6,910.39, its steepest weekly decline in more than 18 months. The index has now fallen more than 10 per cent from its October 6 record high, meeting the technical definition of a market correction. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28 per cent to 22,617.73, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.93 per cent to 48,147.33.The sell-off extended across global markets, with Japan's Nikkei falling 5.06 per cent and South Korea's Kospi losing more than 5 per cent. Taiwan's stock market fell 17 per cent for the week, its biggest weekly decline since 1990. MSCI's global equities gauge shed 8.1 per cent over the week, its steepest drop since early 2020.Chipmakers bore the brunt of Friday's selling. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.7 per cent, while shares of AMD, Micron Technology and Broadcom dropped 13.3 per cent, 13.9 per cent and 12.2 per cent, respectively. Nvidia fell 14 per cent, extending its decline to nine sessions out of the past 10.The pressure reflects growing investor concerns over the high valuations of AI companies, the scale of spending on data centres and whether future earnings will justify the investments. Nvidia has also faced company-specific scrutiny, including a US securities regulator's investigation into its accounting practices and concerns linked to its business dealings with a Singapore-based firm investigated over suspected chip shipments to China."Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, adding that strong AI demand and successful stock listings were no longer enough to sustain investor appetite amid questions over valuations, borrowing costs and corporate profitability.Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI chatbot, also came under pressure in its first full day of trading after its high-profile market debut. Its shares fell 9.1 per cent to $88.30, after dropping as much as 14.5 per cent during the session. The stock remained above its initial public offering price of $83, but was well below its brief peak of $115.10 on Thursday.As investors moved away from riskier assets, US government bonds rallied. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note fell more than 10 basis points to around 4.95 per cent, marking its biggest daily decline since October 22. The 30-year yield also fell, while the two-year yield dropped more than 13 basis points.In commodities, oil prices rose amid concerns over possible attacks linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran and continued tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude settled around $92.61 a barrel, up 0.68 per cent, while US crude gained 1.49 per cent to $83.67.Gold and silver, meanwhile, extended their losses. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after PM Modi shellacked India Inc for not translating tax cuts into more jobs and higher salaries, stunned corporate honchos were still trying to process the rebuke, with many worrying the govt may shut the door on any requests for tax concessions.The "insatiable hunger for concessions" remark by the PM hit members of the industry and businesses at the Ficci event hard. Many sitting in the room only realised the weight of Modi's comment later. Some executives are also seeing it as a signal that govt is in no mood to offer concessions. "It's a signal to back off before the budget," said an industry veteran.In coming weeks, the industry will be readying data to argue how jobs have increased and wages have gone up.Executives pointed to the pressure faced by the industry due to increase in fuel and input costs and the impact of a weak rupee that companies had to grapple with until a few weeks ago. However, sources in govt acknowledged the problems but maintained that the industry could have done much more to reciprocate the help govt extended to help them grow and compete internationally. Frustration with the industry's response had been building up.Officials have argued that from reduction in tax rates, direct as well as GST, to making life easier for businesses, govt had created conditions for the industry to grow at a rapid pace.Modi's statement is seen as a push to lift real incomes, a key worry for employees and workers since Covid. The 2025 Economic Survey had noted that corporate profitability had soared to a 15-year high in 2024 but growth in employee expense moderated.In 2023-24, job growth was estimated at 5.6%, while emoluments rose 11.8% with profits rising 10%, according to the Annual Survey of Industries. The latest report showed that persons engaged was up 7.2% to 2.1 crore in 2024-25, and emoluments were up 12.1% to Rs 8 lakh crore. Profits were up 7.7% to 11.6 lakh crore.Over the past few years, govt and industry have sparred over the pace of investment, with the private sector seen as lagging. articles.summary: “Grand Theft Auto VI” generated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, setting a record for the biggest launch of any entertainment
articles.body: “Grand Theft Auto VI” generated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, setting a record for the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, publisher Rockstar Games said on Friday, as the latest instalment in the blockbuster franchise recorded unprecedented demand after 13 years.The figure was based on the company’s estimates of global sales through the end of Thursday, the day the game was released. Rockstar also said it had sold 32.5 million units before launch, setting a record across platforms.“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you,” Sam Houser, Rockstar’s president and founder, said in a release.The launch substantially surpassed the opening performance of its predecessor, “Grand Theft Auto V”, which was released in 2013. According to Rockstar’s figures, the earlier game generated around $800 million in its first 24 hours, while it took three days to reach $1 billion in retail sales.“GTA V” went on to become one of the best-selling video games of all time. Publisher Take-Two Interactive has said it accounted for more than 230 million of the franchise’s over 470 million units sold worldwide.The $3.79 billion opening also exceeded the approximately $2.9 billion worldwide box-office collection of “Avengers: Endgame”, which regained its position as the highest-grossing film after a re-release.Earlier on Friday, market research firm Sensor Tower estimated that “GTA VI” had generated $2.36 billion in revenue from approximately 24.6 million units sold. Rockstar’s later announcement was based on its own estimates of worldwide first-day retail sales.The game went on sale on Thursday for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with its release beginning in New Zealand and rolling out across markets at midnight local time. PlayStation had earlier said it was working with Rockstar to allow players to preload the title nine days before launch, following record pre-orders on its digital store.Set in Vice City, a fictionalised version of Miami in the state of Leonida, the game follows Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval as they navigate crime and attempts to improve their circumstances. articles.title: In 1984, Indian Railways introduced RAC tickets to prevent arbitrary berth allotments by staff. 43 years later, it may be scrapped as digital checks make system outdated and passengers pay full fare to share one berth
articles.summary: Indian Railways’ Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility for train passengers may have become redundant with the introduction of digital upgrades
articles.body: Indian Railways’ Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) facility for train passengers may have become redundant with the introduction of digital upgrades to Indian Railways’ ticket-checking system, a section of senior railway officials has argued. The debate comes amid reports that the Railway Ministry is considering discontinuing the facility.RAC was introduced in 1983-84 by then Railway Minister ABA Ghani Khan Choudhury, who announced the initiative while presenting the Railway Budget in Parliament.Why was RAC introduced in 1984Explaining the rationale behind the proposal, Choudhury said a fixed number of berths would be set aside for passengers at the top of the waiting list. This would enable them to receive sleeper berths during the journey if passengers holding confirmed reservations failed to turn up, leaving their berths vacant.He also maintained that the system had helped prevent railway staff from allotting berths arbitrarily, according to a PTI report.The Railway Ministry modified the RAC arrangement in 2016 by increasing the number of berths reserved for such passengers. Previously, each sleeper coach had five side-lower berths set aside under RAC, accommodating 10 passengers. The allocation was raised to seven berths, allowing 14 passengers to be accommodated.The allocation was also increased in air-conditioned coaches. In 3AC, the number of side-lower berths reserved for RAC passengers went up from two to four per coach, increasing the capacity from four to eight passengers. In 2AC coaches, the allocation rose from two berths to three, enabling six passengers to be accommodated instead of four.Why RAC ticketing may be scrappedUnder the existing RAC arrangement, two passengers share a single berth, even though both are charged the full fare. The system has faced criticism over the years, particularly over concerns about passengers paying the full ticket price despite having to share a berth, as well as the inconvenience this causes.Officials told PTI that when the reservation and ticketing systems were not digitally linked, RAC was a passenger-friendly initiative. However, digital innovations have changed the scenario.“If a passenger doesn’t turn up, the train ticket examiner (TTE), who carries a Hand Held Terminal (HHT) that is digitally connected to the entire ticketing system, enters the no-show status against that particular berth, and the same berth becomes available for prospective passengers from the next station,” a senior railway official was quoted as saying.According to the official, doing away with RAC would also limit the possibility of unfair practices by TTEs by reducing the discretion they currently exercise.It would require them to finish checking tickets without delay and update the system with the “No Turn-Up” status whenever a passenger fails to board. The vacant berth could then be offered for current booking to passengers boarding at the next station.The official said the Railways no longer incurs a financial loss when passengers fail to undertake their journeys, following changes to ticket cancellation rules in 2015. Under the revised norms, passengers who do not turn up for their journey forfeit the entire fare paid, without receiving any refund.“The same berth is then offered to another passenger at the full fare. So, even if the seat goes vacant, there is no financial loss to the Railways because it has already collected the fare from the original passenger,” the official said.“At the same time, the vacant berth would be offered to other passengers at the next station, ensuring that the facility would not go wasted,” he added.Railway officials also highlighted a recommendation made by the Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee for a partial refund of fares paid by RAC passengers.In its report tabled in the Lok Sabha on February 4, 2026, the committee said charging the full fare to RAC ticket holders who remained in the RAC category even after the reservation chart was prepared, without receiving a full berth, could not be justified.The panel recommended that the Railway Ministry develop a system to refund part of the fare to passengers who paid the full amount when booking but were not allotted an entire berth. Officials, however, said designing such a mechanism would be complicated because tickets are booked through both online e-ticketing platforms and physical reservation counters.Currently, RAC is not available on Vande Bharat Sleeper trains. Their fares are 30% to 95% higher than those of other trains operating on the same routes.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.body: MUMBAI: Record foreign buying pushed the sensex up 898 points, or 1.1%, on Friday to 83,920, its highest close in nine months, taking foreign portfolio inflows in Nov past Rs 1.3 lakh crore, an all-time high for monthly flows. FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 10,308 crore on Friday, BSE data showed, adding to the Rs 1.2 lakh crore invested till Thursday, according to NSDL data.The buying lifted the rupee to 92.67 against the dollar, nearly 4.5% above its record low of 96.96 in May. The currency gained around 1.75% this week from 94.3.Sensex has gained over 9,300 points, or nearly 13%, this month even as global AI-linked stocks came under pressure. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has fallen over 6% and South Korea's Kospi has declined around 15%. Nifty rose 286 points to close at 25,801. Friday's rally added around Rs 2.2 lakh crore to investor wealth, taking the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 514.2 lakh crore, or around $5.5 trillion. Private banks led the gains, with the BSE Bankex and NSE Bank Nifty scaling record highs.According to market participants, strong foreign inflows and a shift away from global AI-linked investments supported the rupee. "The rupee witnessed a strong rally, gaining around 0.75% to 92.66... Strong foreign fund flows continue to provide support to the domestic currency," said a market expert, who expects the currency to trade between 92.25 and 93 in the near term.Foreign exchange reserves, however, fell by more than $14 billion week-on-week to $705.3 billion in the week ended Nov 13, their lowest level in about three months, RBI data released on Friday showed. Foreign currency assets declined by $7.8 billion and gold holdings by $6.1 billion.According to Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments, foreign investors shifting away from global AI trades supported private banks, while easing concerns over AI disruption helped Indian IT stocks. articles.title: Noel asks for recordings of Tata Sons meet again
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Noel Tata on Friday once again sought video recordings of the Sept 17 Tata Sons meetings that culminated in N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as
articles.body: MUMBAI: Noel Tata on Friday once again sought video recordings of the Sept 17 Tata Sons meetings that culminated in N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman. The company had rejected his demand earlier on grounds that it was not legally required to retain or share recordings of in-person meetings with directors.The Tata Trusts chairman, who is also a director of Tata Sons, has now asked the company to "preserve" the recordings of both the nomination and remuneration committee (NRC) meeting and the board meeting held that day.Noel also disputed the minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting and reiterated his position that no resolution on Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third term had been validly passed as per Tata Sons' articles of association.While Tata Sons had listed an update from the NRC as an agenda item for the Sept 17 board meeting, Noel maintained that the reappointment resolution was taken up under a "debrief from the NRC". He also contended that the NRC minutes circulated to him were only a draft and did not bear signatures of committee members.The final minutes of the Sept 17 board meeting will come up for approval at the Tata Sons board's Nov 26 meeting, where directors can either approve them or record their objections.Noel has also renewed his objection to Tata Sons' filing with the Registrar of Companies on Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five years under Section 117 of the Companies Act, which mandates that companies file certain board resolutions within a 30-day window.Noel has also renewed his conflict-of-interest objection over the business relationship between TVS Motor Co, associated with Venu Srinivasan, and Hanno One Warehousing, a company linked to members of N Chandrasekaran's family. Noel's contention is that Srinivasan, a Tata Trusts trustee and Tata Sons director, should have recused himself from the NRC proceedings that considered Chandrasekaran's reappointment. Srinivasan backed the reappointment, with his vote giving Chandrasekaran the support of both a majority of the board and one of the two Trust-nominee directors.Tata Sons had rejected the conflict-of-interest argument, saying Hanno One has no transactions with Tata Sons or any Tata group entity. articles.summary: Retail investors who rushed to buy Anthropic shares following its initial public offering (IPO) faced losses on Friday as the stock plunged 13%, reversing
articles.body: Retail investors who rushed to buy Anthropic shares following its initial public offering (IPO) faced losses on Friday as the stock plunged 13%, reversing much of its gains on the first day of trading.The shares, which opened at $112 on Thursday against an IPO price of $83, closed at $97 before falling to $85 by 12:20 pm ET (1720 GMT) on Friday, according to LSEG data.The sharp decline came after retail investors recorded more than $750 million in Anthropic share transactions on Thursday, marking the highest turnover for a stock debut in Vanda Research's records. The figure surpassed the $670 million recorded for SpaceX during its IPO in June.Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Thursday in what the report described as the biggest IPO in history, giving public market investors their first opportunity to invest in a leading artificial intelligence company.The strong retail interest also resulted in the third-largest day of net retail buying for a stock on its debut in records dating back to 2012, according to Vanda Research. However, net buying remained below the records set by SpaceX, at $118 million, and Coinbase, at $92 million."Different investors are different but most will be willing to look through the short-term volatility and focus on the bigger future," Viraj Patel, global macro strategist at Vanda, said of Anthropic.Anthropic said that less than 20% of its shares were allocated to retail investors. A person involved in the offering said the allocation was slightly lower than initially expected because of strong demand from institutional investors.In the United Kingdom, around 3.6 million shares worth approximately $300 million were allocated to retail investors, according to RetailBook, which coordinated the offering.British investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown said its clients received 34% of the shares they had requested, in line with allocations made through other platforms.A European retail investment platform said Anthropic's trading volume, number of traders and average order size on its first day were lower than those recorded for SpaceX.The decline in Anthropic shares coincided with a broader fall in global stocks on Friday as investor sentiment towards artificial intelligence weakened.Investors are increasingly seeking stronger returns from the massive investments being made in AI model training, computing infrastructure and data centre expansion.The concerns have raised questions about whether companies investing heavily in artificial intelligence will be able to generate sufficient returns to justify their expenditure.Anthropic and SpaceX have reserved a larger share of their IPO offerings for retail investors, with SpaceX allocating around 20% to smaller investors.Traditionally, IPO allocations have favoured institutional investors, with a 90:10 split between institutional and retail investors, according to Fidelity.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Systematic withdrawal: EPFO seeks income tax tweaks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: EPFO is seeking amendments in the Income Tax Act to ensure that monthly payouts under its newly approved systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: EPFO is seeking amendments in the Income Tax Act to ensure that monthly payouts under its newly approved systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) are legally recognised as staged withdrawals, and not as a pension, while also proposing to delink provident fund (PF) membership from traditional employer-employee relationship.The retirement body wants clarity that periodic installments drawn by retirees - whether drawn monthly, quarterly or annually - are treated solely as a systematic drawdown of their own accumulated savings balance rather than an annuity or pension payout. PF withdrawals at present are structured around final lump-sum settlements upon retirement."The matter has been conveyed to the ministry to pursue the matter with the finance ministry. The approval is expected to come soon, with SWP operationalisation kicking soon," a person familiar with the development told TOI. Under SWP, retiring members are being provided with the opportunity to withdraw only a part of their PF corpus and earn interest on the remaining amount. The facility will not be available to members of exempted PF trusts in the initial phase.In order to enable social security coverage for the vast unorganised workers, EPFO has also proposed breaking the link between PF participation and formal payroll employment. Under existing norms, active EPF membership and contributions are tied to an employer-employee relationship. EPFO wants the framework amended so that retired members, platform workers and unorganised sector labourers can continue as active members and contribute independently. The retirement fund body has also sought to remove the requirement that PF contributions must originate from "salary". Since gig workers, unorganised labourers and retirees do not earn conventional monthly wages, the amendment will allow them to deposit irregular earnings directly into their Universal Account Number (UAN), while enabling third-party micro-contributions such as incentives or customer tips.To make solo retirement saving viable where there is no matching employer share, EPFO has requested raising annual contribution limit for self or third-party deposits to Rs 5 lakh, bringing it on a par with the general provident fund threshold for govt employees.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Lower tariff: Scotch companies caught in category flipping
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Scotch lobby may be making noise over tariffs not coming down for bulk whisky despite the India-UK trade agreement, but it is slowly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Scotch lobby may be making noise over tariffs not coming down for bulk whisky despite the India-UK trade agreement, but it is slowly emerging that the Scotch makers industry not only knew about the classification problems but also had got into litigation over the product code used to import at lower duties, which has now come back to haunt them.While govt officials maintain that India will honour its commitment and they are engaged to find a solution. The problem has its origins in product classification. As part of the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, govt has offered to allow bulk whisky classified as 220830 (six-digit product classification) at 75% tariff, while 220890, which stands for other unadulterated ethyl alcohol, attracts 110% duty. Unlike what the Scotch makers are claiming, no duty concession has been offered to products falling under classification 2106.Over three decades ago, Bussa Overseas and subsequently Pernod Ricard in 2008 challenged the classification. While Bussa argued that the product should be classified under tariff heading 220810 as it involved the import of bulk concentrates with 60-61% alcoholic strength, given the tariff advantage (this entry was later moved to 210690). Customs wanted it classified as finished potable spirits under heading 220830 but lost the case.With the trade deal in place, and 2106 outside the scope of concessions, the Scotch industry is seeking to flip the product classification from heading 2106 to 220890 - something that they woke up to after negotiators from both sides had finalised the agreement."A key concern for our industry is ensuring the inclusion of all our product's relevant tariff codes within the tariff liberalisation schedule. This includes those utilised for the export of bulk whisky products... Tariff code 22089099, which is currently used for the majority of bulk Scotch Whisky exports for regulatory reasons, was not liberalised to the same extent as the Scotch Whisky specific tariff codes, despite industry raising the importance of this," Scotch Whisky Association said in its submission to a parliamentary panel in the UK in Aug 2025."As things currently stand, this potentially means a significant proportion of Scotch Whisky exports will not benefit from the agreed tariff liberalisation, undermining the opportunities of this deal for the industry, as well as for the Indian industry which utilises bulk Scotch Whisky, either for bottling in country or as an ingredient in other products. The SWA underscored the importance of these specific inclusions throughout the negotiation process. This highlights the need for close, consistent, and meaningful business engagement throughout all stages of negotiations, including access to draft text, in order to avoid such situations from arising," it added.When caught seeking to reclassify bulk Scotch from 2106 to 220830 to take the tariff advantage, companies and industry bodies representing them sought to blame Indian customs authorities.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The core sector grew 10.9% in Oct, driven by strong performance in the electricity, cement, iron ore and coal industries along with a favourable base effect, official data released Friday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 8.2% in Sept. This is the strongest performance of the core sector in the new series with the revised base year.During April-Oct, the core sector has grown 6% as compared to 2.3% a year ago. Output in the energy-dominant industries like natural gas (-7.6%), crude oil (-4.1%) and fertilisers (-12.2%) saw continued sequential contraction in Oct, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia. Output in the refinery products (3.4%), though positive, saw sequential deceleration during the month.Output in the infrastructure-dominant industries such as electricity (21.6%), cement (15.4%), iron ore (26.4%) and steel (7.3%) showed sequential acceleration in Oct, reflecting the divergence in the growth trajectory of energy dominant and infrastructure dominant industries in recent months due to volatile crude prices.The core sector accounts for 40% weight in the index of industrial production (IIP) and is considered as a precursor of the performance of the country's wider industrial sector.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Greater synergy and integration between Air India and AI Express have emerged as a major way to cut costs, amid spiralling losses.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Greater synergy and integration between Air India and AI Express have emerged as a major way to cut costs, amid spiralling losses. At an Air India board meet here Friday chaired by N Chandrasekaran, the focus was on reducing losses as the AI group has lost over Rs 50,000 crore in just under five years after returning to the Tata fold and the promised capital-intensive revival is a bit distant in the future. Integration of roles at the full service and budget airlines to cut costs, rationalisation of loss-making routes and optimising revenue and fuel efficiency were the key focus areas at the meet. Some important decisions are likely to be conveyed to employees at a town hall that could be convened soon, say sources.Air India's loss widened to more than Rs 22,000 crore in FY26 due to multiple factors like fuel price rise, rupee depreciation and airspace closure restrictions that make western routes longer. AI's USP is being the only Indian carrier as of now that provides direct connectivity to faraway North America, Europe, Far East and Australia. With western routes affected, this USP can't be capitalised to the hilt.The board discussed operational and financial matters, to ensure operations are more cost-effective. A significant focus was on increasing fuel efficiency. Air India's new chief executive and MD Tewolde Gebremariam had earlier this month shared his plans for the airline's revival that sees more wide-body aircraft and a battle on costs. He feels AI has "punched below its weight" for too long and should "regain market share from competition (foreign airlines)" as that "business belongs to AI."While the "short term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the deep-in-the-red airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency.For this plan, Tewolde sought the board's approval on Friday, a day after the Tata top brass led by Noel Tata and Chandrasekaran visited the airline and aviation academy in Gurgaon.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: MUMBAI: Hours after chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said that the markets regulator was in the process of coming out with a consultation paper on foreign
articles.body: MUMBAI: Hours after chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said that the markets regulator was in the process of coming out with a consultation paper on foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), Sebi published a paper saying it intends to do away with the stringent rule relating to the additional disclosure framework (ADF). This requires select FPIs to disclose granular details relating to who all have invested in their funds that are invested in India.A comparative analysis of various jurisdictions around the world showed that Sebi's rules were more stringent than others. In addition, Sebi also asks for an additional disclosure framework (ADF) under which select FPIs are "required to submit granular details of all entities holding any ownership, economic interest, or exercising control in the FPI, on a full look through basis, up to the level of all natural persons, without any threshold."Sebi's own research showed that granular disclosure requirements under ADF were unique to India. "Disclosure requirements that are not in line with globally accepted practices could potentially place India at a competitive disadvantage vis-a-vis peer jurisdictions with relatively lenient regulatory requirements," the paper said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Woman earns Rs 6.7 lakh, including Rs 3.9 lakh short-term capital gains; taxman denies Rs 25,000 Section 87A rebate under new regime, demands Rs 75,502 tax; ITAT grants relief, but a catch applies this year
articles.summary: Are your short-term capital gains also eligible for a rebate if your overall income falls below Rs 12 lakh?
articles.body: Are your short-term capital gains also eligible for a rebate if your overall income falls below Rs 12 lakh? A taxpayer who earned short-term capital gains from listed equity shares has won a dispute over a Rs 25,000 income tax rebate after the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Hyderabad, held in her favour.The ITAT decision was regarding the availability of rebate under Section 87A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (the ‘Act’), against tax payable on short-term capital gains arising from the transfer of equity shares taxable under Section 111A of Act.In its November 6, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that Section 87A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, did not expressly prohibit the rebate in cases where income included short-term capital gains taxable at a special rate under Section 111A. However, there is a catch.What the case is aboutA woman filed her income tax return for assessment year 2025-26, declaring a total income of Rs 6,77,511. This included short-term capital gains of Rs 3,97,511 arising from the transfer of listed equity shares. Such gains are taxable u/s 111A of the Act at a special rate of tax.She opted for the new tax regime under Section 115BAC(1A) and claimed a rebate of Rs 25,000 under Section 87A. However, when the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru, processed her return, it determined a tax payable at Rs 75,502 without allowing the rebate.The assessee challenged the denial before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals). The first appellate authority rejected her explanation and upheld the denial. She then approached the Hyderabad bench of the ITAT.Her authorised representative argued that neither Section 87A nor Section 115BAC(1A) expressly barred the rebate merely because part of the taxpayer’s income was taxable under Section 111A.The representative also relied on two earlier tribunal decisions: Jayshreeben Jayantibhai Palsana v. ITO, decided by the ITAT Ahmedabad bench, and Pushpa Prakash Misar v. ITO, decided by the ITAT Mumbai bench. Jayendran’s counsel additionally cited the Bombay High Court decision in Chamber of Tax Consultants v. DGIT (Systems).The Revenue opposed the appeal. Its representative relied on CBDT Circular No. 13/2025, dated September 19, 2025, and argued that the rebate was not applicable to taxpayers opting for the new tax regime under Section 115BAC(1A). The department maintained that the lower authorities had correctly rejected the claim.Why did ITAT rule in favour of assessee?Tanu Gupta, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP says that this judgement is important for the interpretation of Section 87A and the extent to which the rebate can be restricted by Circular No. 13/2025 dated September 19, 2025 issued by the CBDT.“ITAT was of the opinion that AO and CIT(A) did not have any other reason to disallow the tax rebate u/s 87A of the Act from the tax liability which included tax on short-term capital gains u/s 111A at a special rate,” she says.Further, on observing the plain language of Section 87A and its provisos, the ITAT was of the opinion that there is no restriction to claim rebate u/s.87A of the Act where the assessee satisfies the other prescribed conditions, such as income being under the applicable threshold even if it includes income taxable at special rate under Section 111A of the Act.“The Tribunal's decision also relies on past judgments. It was held that there is no express restriction to claim rebate u/s.87A of the Act even in a case of tax payment under the new regime of taxation as per provisions of Sec.115BAC(1A) of the Act,” Gupta tells TOI.“The ruling is a welcome development for taxpayers, particularly for earlier assessment years, as it clarifies that the eligibility for tax rebate must be decided based on the provisions of the Income-tax Act and not restricted by administrative circulars or changes in the return filing utility. It also reinforces the principle that a circular cannot take away a benefit that is available under the Act,” she adds.However, Gupta cautions that taxpayers should note that the position changes from FY 2025-26 onwards, as the Finance Act, 2025 has expressly restricted the Section 87A rebate to tax calculated at the specified slab rates. “Accordingly, the rebate will no longer be available against tax payable on special-rate income, including short-term capital gains under Section 111A,” she concludes.Hence, even though ITAT ruled in favour of the assessee for that particular assessment year, taxpayers should not that this rebate is no longer applicable from this year.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Zohran Mamdani makes surprise appearance on CNN’s ‘Have I Got News for You’
articles.summary: “We’re gonna have someone fun come out,” Roy Wood Jr. told the studio audience for CNN’s comedy panel show “Have I Got News for You” on Friday afternoon.
articles.body: “We’re gonna have someone fun come out,” Roy Wood Jr. told the studio audience for CNN’s comedy panel show “Have I Got News for You” on Friday afternoon. Judging by the cheers and applause, the audience was happily surprised by what happened next. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani joined Wood on stage for a jovial conversation about politics, including the Senate leadership race and the mayor’s much-scrutinized relationship with President Donald Trump. The episode, which will air Saturday at 9 p.m. Eastern on CNN, demonstrated the in-demand mayor’s unconventional approach to media appearances While he hasn’t appeared on “Saturday Night Live,” he dropped by “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” when Kimmel was in Brooklyn last September, and made a cameo on “The Tonight Show” soon after his inauguration in January. “This is crazy. I was actually here to see John Oliver,” Mamdani joked during the CNN taping, knowing that Oliver’s HBO show is taped in the same building on the far west side of Manhattan. The timing of Friday’s “Have I Got News for You” visit was notable for a couple of reasons. First, it was one of Mamdani’s first interviews since the Democratic Party retook control of Congress in the midterm elections; second, it was slightly complicated by the fact that Mamdani is on crutches right now. On Thursday evening, the mayor sustained an injury during a soccer game with members of the New York City press corps. “I tore my Achilles,” he told reporters at a press conference Friday morning. “Have I Got News for You” producers worried that he might cancel, but Mamdani still participated in the taping, seated at the table with his crutches kept off-screen. “I got scared when you showed up, because usually when you show up in New York, it’s to fix something,” Wood said, making a joke about his own job security. Then Wood and his panelists pretended to continue with the show as planned, beginning with the question, “Can Mamdani pull off this mustache?” The mayor explained that he is participating in “Movember” to raise awareness about men’s health issues. Panelist Amber Ruffin sounded smitten. “You’re Homecoming king right now,” she quipped. “And maybe, always?” The comedians offered theories about Trump’s unexpectedly cordial working relationship with Mamdani. “It’s like, you know that old Life cereal commercial? ‘Mikey hates everything, but he likes Life.’ I feel like that’s Trump with you,” panelist Michael Ian Black said. Mamdani posited that “the one thing we do have in common is this city,” given Trump is a native New Yorker; whenever they talk, the mayor said, “I try and focus our conversations around housing, how to build more housing.” Mamdani let the professionals crack most of the jokes. When the show turned to Michigan’s Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who recently urged Trump to embrace Medicare for All as “Trumpcare,” Black remarked, “If Trump goes for El-Sayed’s pitch, and he’s a fan of yours, is there any chance we could convert him to Islam?” Mamdani laughed, smiled and waited a beat while thinking about what to say. “It’s never come up in our conversations,” he responded. Mamdani also weighed in on Sen. Chris Van Hollen’s challenge against Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Schumer declined to endorse Mamdani for mayor last year, and Mamdani hasn’t backed Schumer in the majority leader contest. Black asked him: “Do you have a preference?” “I think less about who it should be and more about what they should do,” Mamdani said, arguing that “the point of power is to use it, to deliver.” Mamdani stayed on message and avoided direct criticism of Schumer. Later in the conversation, he said, “I don’t think grudges are worth holding, because grudges don’t pay people’s bills. And to me, I think that our politics has to be, how do we help New Yorkers pay their bills?”

articles.title: India vs US interest rates: Trump cites 'look at India' example to turn up heat on Fed
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised the Federal Reserve over its interest rate policy, citing India's economic growth as an example of how
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised the Federal Reserve over its interest rate policy, citing India's economic growth as an example of how lower borrowing costs could support expansion. He argued that the US economy could achieve growth of 15-20% if the central bank reduced interest rates.Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump accused the Federal Reserve of being "very political" and alleged that it raised borrowing costs whenever the US announced strong economic figures, rather than lowering rates to support further growth."Interest rates are too high because we have a very political Fed. I'm not blaming the chairman, but the fact that we have a very political Fed. Whenever we announce good numbers, they raise the interest rates. They do that for a reason. It should be the opposite," Trump said.He argued that strong economic performance should allow the central bank to reduce interest rates because better economic indicators reflected improved creditworthiness. Trump also claimed that the Fed's approach was restricting America's economic potential."We do just the opposite. We do it to destroy the country. When we have these great numbers, you shouldn't keep raising the rates. You should lower rates because we're a better credit. We would have a GDP of 15 or 20 per cent, not 4 per cent. We'd pay off the debt very rapidly. That's the way it should work. But we do it in reverse," he said.Trump compares US interest rates with IndiaDrawing a comparison with India, Trump pointed to the country's economic growth and monetary policy, arguing that the US could achieve a much higher growth rate if borrowing costs were reduced."If you look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a 7 per cent GDP. We'd have a 14%, 15%, maybe even a 20% GDP. It's really a sad thing when you do so great and then they (Fed) raise the interest rate. The fact is, we've blown through it," the US President said.However, the latest official monetary policy figures show that India's benchmark interest rate is higher than that of the US.According to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) October 7 monetary policy decision, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) increased the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. The standing deposit facility rate was set at 5.25%, while the marginal standing facility rate and bank rate were raised to 5.75%.In comparison, the US Federal Reserve maintained its federal funds target range at 3.75%-4% in its October 28 policy decision.This means India's benchmark repo rate is 1.50 to 1.75 percentage points higher than the US federal funds target range. The two rates are not identical instruments, but they provide a broad comparison of the monetary policy benchmarks in the two economies.India vs US: How do their GDP growth rates compare?India's latest official GDP data also provides context to Trump's reference to the country's economic performance.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), India's real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-27, covering April to June 2026.In the US, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that real GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, covering July to September. This followed growth of 2.2% in the second quarter.However, the two growth figures use different measurement periods and conventions. India's 7.8% represents year-on-year growth, while the US figure of 3.4% is a seasonally adjusted annualised quarterly growth rate.The figures therefore provide an indication of the two economies' recent performance but are not directly comparable without adjusting for these differences.Why are the Fed and RBI following different interest rate policies?The difference in interest rates reflects the distinct economic conditions and monetary policy priorities of the two countries.The Federal Reserve operates under a dual mandate of achieving maximum employment and maintaining price stability. Its long-term inflation target is 2%.According to the US Bureau of Economic Analysis, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, rose 3.6% year-on-year in September 2026. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 3.1%.Both measures remained above the Federal Reserve's 2% inflation target, providing an important consideration for its monetary policy decisions.In India, the RBI's monetary policy framework focuses on maintaining price stability while keeping growth objectives in mind. The central bank's inflation target is 4%, with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%.The RBI's October decision to increase the repo rate by 25 basis points also reflected its assessment of inflationary risks and broader economic conditions.Trump calls for lowest interest rates in USTrump further argued that the US should have the lowest interest rates globally, citing its position in the international economy and its contribution to the financial success of other countries.Explaining his position, he said, "We're the country that makes other countries successful. Some of them are considered financial elite, but they are not. They are only elite because of us. So we should have the lowest."Trump has repeatedly criticised the Federal Reserve's monetary policy, arguing that high borrowing costs restrict economic expansion and increase the government's debt-servicing burden.However, the central bank's decisions are based on its assessment of inflation, employment and broader economic conditions, rather than GDP growth alone.Money habits form by age 7.
